title.zh: 卷四十五 列傳第三十五 王敬則 陳顯達 張敬兒 崔慧景
title.en: Volume 45 Biographies 35: Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Zhang Jing'er, Cui Huijing
title.raw: 卷四十五 列傳第三十五 王敬則 陳顯達 張敬兒 崔慧景 Volume 45 Biographies 35: Wang Jingze, Chen Xianda, Zhang Jing'er, Cui Huijing

sentences.zh: 王敬則

translations.literal: Wang Jingze
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze

sentences.zh: 王敬則，臨淮射陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Jingze was a native of Sheyang in Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze was a native of Sheyang in Linhuai commandery.

sentences.zh: 僑居晉陵南沙縣。

translations.literal: His family had moved and settled in Nansha County in Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: His family had relocated and settled in Nansha County in Jinling.

sentences.zh: 母為女巫，常謂人云：「敬則生時胞衣紫色，應得鳴鼓角。

translations.literal: His mother was a shamaness and often told people, "When Jingze was born his afterbirth was purple; he ought to sound drums and horns."
translations.idiomatic: His mother was a shamaness and often told people, "When Jingze was born his afterbirth was purple—he was destined to command drums and horns."

sentences.zh: 」人笑之曰：「汝子得為人吹角可矣。」

translations.literal: People laughed at her and said, "Your son might manage to blow a horn for someone."
translations.idiomatic: People laughed at her and said, "Your son might at best earn his keep blowing a horn for someone."

sentences.zh: 敬則年長，而兩腋下生乳，各長數寸。

translations.literal: When Jingze grew up, breasts formed under both armpits, each several inches long.
translations.idiomatic: As Jingze grew older, breasts formed under both armpits, each several inches long.

sentences.zh: 夢騎五色師子。

translations.literal: He dreamed of riding a five-colored lion.
translations.idiomatic: He once dreamed that he was riding a five-colored lion.

sentences.zh: 性倜儻不羈，好刀劍，嘗與暨陽縣吏鬥，謂曰：「我若得暨陽縣，當鞭汝小吏背。

translations.literal: By nature he was unrestrained and free-spirited, fond of blades; he once fought with a clerk of Jiyang County and said to him, "If I ever get Jiyang County, I shall flog your clerkly back."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and unrestrained, fond of swords and knives. He once brawled with a clerk of Jiyang County and told him, "If I ever become magistrate of Jiyang, I will flog your clerkly back."

sentences.zh: 」吏唾其面曰：「汝得暨陽縣，我亦得司徒公矣。

translations.literal: The clerk spat in his face and said, "If you get Jiyang County, I shall become Minister over the Masses."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk spat in his face and said, "If you get Jiyang County, I might as well become Minister over the Masses."

sentences.zh: 」屠狗商販，遍于三吳。

translations.literal: He butchered dogs and traded as a peddler throughout the Three Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: He butchered dogs and peddled goods all across the Three Wu region.

sentences.zh: 使于高麗，與其國女子私通，因不肯還，被收錄然後反。

translations.literal: On a mission to Goguryeo he had an affair with a woman of that country and, because he refused to return, was arrested and only then came back.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Goguryeo he took a Goguryeo woman as his lover and refused to return home; he was detained and only then sent back.

sentences.zh: 敬則少時於草中射獵，有蟲如烏豆集其身，擿去乃脫，其處皆流血。

translations.literal: When young, Jingze was hunting in the grass when insects like black beans clustered on his body; when picked off they came away and every spot bled.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Jingze was hunting in the grass when insects the size of black beans swarmed over him; when he picked them off they came away with his skin and every spot bled.

sentences.zh: 敬則惡之，詣道士卜，道士曰：「此封侯瑞也。

translations.literal: Jingze took this as an ill omen and went to a Daoist for divination; the Daoist said, "This is an auspice of enfeoffment as marquis."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze took this as a bad sign and consulted a Daoist priest, who said, "This is an omen that you will be enfeoffed as a marquis."

sentences.zh: 」敬則聞之喜，故出都自效。

translations.literal: Jingze was pleased to hear this and therefore left the capital to offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze was delighted to hear this and left the capital to seek his fortune in government service.

sentences.zh: 後補暨陽令，昔日鬥吏亡叛，勒令出，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed magistrate of Jiyang; the clerk with whom he had once fought had fled as a rebel and was ordered to come forward, and Jingze treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was appointed magistrate of Jiyang. The clerk with whom he had once brawled had fled and joined the rebels, but when he was ordered to surrender, Jingze received him with great kindness.

sentences.zh: 曰：「我已得暨陽縣，汝何時得司徒公邪？

translations.literal: He said, "I have already got Jiyang County—when will you become Minister over the Masses?"
translations.idiomatic: He said to him, "I have Jiyang County now—when will you become Minister over the Masses?"

sentences.zh: 」初至暨陽縣陸主山下，宗侶十餘船同發，敬則船獨不進，乃令弟入水推之，見烏漆棺。

translations.literal: When he first reached Jiyang County below Mount Luzhu, more than ten boats of kinsmen and companions set out together, but Jingze's boat alone would not advance; he had his younger brother go into the water to push it and they saw a black-lacquered coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When he first arrived at Jiyang below Mount Luzhu, more than ten boats of kinsmen set out together, but Jingze's alone would not move forward. He had his younger brother dive in to push it and they found a black-lacquered coffin.

sentences.zh: 敬則祝云：「若是吉，使船速進，吾富貴當改葬爾。

translations.literal: Jingze prayed, "If this is auspicious, let the boat advance quickly; when I am rich and honored I shall rebury you."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze prayed, "If this is a good omen, let the boat move on at once; when I am rich and honored I will give you a proper reburial."

sentences.zh: 」船須臾去，入縣收此棺葬之。

translations.literal: The boat shortly moved on; upon entering the county he recovered this coffin and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: The boat moved on at once. After he took office in the county he recovered the coffin and buried it properly.

sentences.zh: 時軍荒後，縣有一部劫逃入山中為人患，敬則遣人致意劫帥使出首，當相申論。

translations.literal: At that time, after the military disorders, a band of robbers in the county had fled into the mountains and become a menace; Jingze sent someone to tell the robber chief to surrender and that they would settle matters fairly.
translations.idiomatic: In the aftermath of the military disorders, a band of robbers in the county had fled into the mountains and become a scourge. Jingze sent word to their leader that if he surrendered, they could settle matters fairly.

sentences.zh: 郭下廟神甚酷烈，百姓信之，敬則引神為誓，必不相負。

translations.literal: The deity of the temple below the city wall was very stern, and the common people trusted it; Jingze invoked the god in his oath that he would certainly not betray them.
translations.idiomatic: The local temple god was feared as stern and the people trusted in him; Jingze swore by the god that he would not betray them.

sentences.zh: 劫帥既出，敬則於廟中設酒會，於坐收縛曰：「吾啟神，若負誓，還神十牛。

translations.literal: Once the robber chief had come out, Jingze set a feast in the temple and at the gathering seized and bound them, saying, "I told the god that if I broke my oath I would repay the god ten oxen."
translations.idiomatic: After the robber chief came out, Jingze held a feast in the temple and at the table seized and bound them, saying, "I told the god that if I broke my oath I would repay him with ten oxen."

sentences.zh: 今不得違誓。

translations.literal: Now I cannot break the oath.
translations.idiomatic: Now I cannot break that oath.

sentences.zh: 」即殺十牛解神，並斬諸劫，百姓悅之。

translations.literal: He immediately killed ten oxen as an offering to the god and also beheaded all the robbers; the common people were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately slaughtered ten oxen as an offering to the god and beheaded all the robbers as well, to the great satisfaction of the people.

sentences.zh: 元徽二年，隨齊高帝拒桂陽賊於新亭，敬則與羽林監陳顯達、甯朔將軍高道慶乘舸迎戰，大破賊水軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhui he followed Emperor Gao of Qi to resist the Guiyang rebels at Xinting; Jingze, together with the Feathered Forest commandant Chen Xianda and the Ningshuo general Gao Daoqing, took boats to meet the attack and greatly defeated the rebel river force.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhui, he followed Emperor Gao of Qi to resist the Guiyang rebels at Xinting. Jingze, together with the Feathered Forest commandant Chen Xianda and Ningshuo general Gao Daoqing, took boats to meet them in battle and routed the rebel fleet.

sentences.zh: 事甯，帶南泰山太守、右俠轂主，轉越騎校尉、安成王車騎參軍。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he concurrently held the posts of Administrator of Southern Mount Tai and Right Master of the Chariot Axle, then was transferred to Commandant of the Rapid-as-Leopards Cavalry and Cavalry-and-Chariots Attendant of the Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was restored he concurrently served as Administrator of Southern Mount Tai and Right Master of the Chariot Axle, then was transferred to Commandant of the Rapid-as-Leopards Cavalry and Cavalry-and-Chariots Attendant of the Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王狂虐，左右不自安。

translations.literal: The Prince of Cangwu was violent and cruel, and those around him could not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei of Cangwu was violent and cruel, and those around him lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 敬則以高帝有威名，歸誠奉事，每下直輒往領軍府。

translations.literal: Jingze, because Emperor Gao had a reputation for authority, submitted to him in sincerity and after each shift would go to the Commandant of the Army's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze, impressed by Emperor Gao's reputation for authority, pledged himself to him and after every shift went straight to the commandant's residence.

sentences.zh: 夜著青衣，扶匐道路，為高帝聽察。

translations.literal: At night he wore blue clothes and crawled along the roads to listen and observe for Emperor Gao.
translations.idiomatic: At night he dressed in plain blue clothes and crept along the roads to spy for Emperor Gao.

sentences.zh: 高帝令敬則於殿內伺機。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao had Jingze wait inside the palace for an opportunity.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao stationed Jingze inside the palace to watch for an opportunity.

sentences.zh: 及楊玉夫將首投敬則，敬則馳謁高帝，乃戎服入宮。

translations.literal: When Yang Yufu brought the head and handed it to Jingze, Jingze galloped to report to Emperor Gao and then entered the palace in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yufu brought the emperor's head and handed it to Jingze, Jingze galloped to report to Emperor Gao and then entered the palace in armor.

sentences.zh: 至承明門，門郎疑非蒼梧還，敬則慮人覘見，以刀環塞窐孔，呼開門甚急。

translations.literal: At the Chenming Gate the gate officer suspected this was not Cangwu returning; Jingze feared someone might spy through the opening and stuffed the hole with his sword ring, urgently calling for the gate to be opened.
translations.idiomatic: At the Chenming Gate the gatekeeper suspected this was not Emperor Fei returning. Jingze, fearing someone might peer through the wicket, blocked the opening with his sword ring and urgently demanded that the gate be opened.

sentences.zh: 衛尉丞顏靈寶窺見高帝乘馬在外，竊謂親人：「今若不開內領軍，天下會是亂爾。

translations.literal: The aide of the Commandant of the Guards Yan Lingbao glimpsed Emperor Gao mounted outside and whispered to his kin, "If we do not now admit the Commandant of the Army within, the realm will surely fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lingbao, aide to the Commandant of the Guards, caught sight of Emperor Gao waiting on horseback outside and whispered to his kin, "If we do not admit the commandant of the army now, the realm will fall into chaos."

sentences.zh: 」門開，敬則隨帝入殿。

translations.literal: The gate was opened and Jingze followed the emperor into the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The gate was opened, and Jingze followed the emperor into the hall.

sentences.zh: 敬則不識書，止下名，然甚善決斷。

translations.literal: Jingze could not read and could only sign his name, yet he was very good at making decisions.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze was illiterate and could sign only his name, yet he was remarkably decisive.

sentences.zh: 齊台建，為中領軍。

translations.literal: When the Qi regime was established he became Commandant of the Army for the Center.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qi regime was established he was appointed Commandant of the Army for the Center.

sentences.zh: 高帝將受禪，材官薦易太極殿柱。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao was about to receive the abdication, the craftsmen recommended replacing the pillars of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao was about to receive the abdication, the craftsmen recommended replacing the pillars of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 順帝欲避上，不肯出宮遜位。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun wished to avoid yielding to his superior and refused to leave the palace to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun wished to avoid yielding to his superior and refused to leave the palace to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 明日當臨軒，順帝又逃宮內。

translations.literal: The next day, when he was to appear before the throne, Emperor Shun again fled within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when he was to appear before the throne, Emperor Shun again hid himself inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 敬則將輿入迎帝，啟譬令出，引令升車。

translations.literal: Jingze brought in a carriage to welcome the emperor, urged and exhorted him to come out, and led him to mount the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze brought in a carriage to fetch the emperor, urged him to come out, and helped him into the carriage.

sentences.zh: 順帝不肯即上，收淚謂敬則曰：「欲見殺乎？

translations.literal: Emperor Shun would not mount at once; holding back tears he said to Jingze, "Do you mean to have me killed?"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun would not get in at once. Holding back tears he said to Jingze, "Do you mean to have me killed?"

sentences.zh: 」敬則答曰：「出居別宮爾，官先取司馬家亦復如此。

translations.literal: Jingze answered, "You will only move to another palace; the court earlier took the house of Sima in just the same way."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze answered, "You will only move to another palace—the court did the same when it took over the house of Sima."

sentences.zh: 」順帝泣而彈指：「唯願後身生生世世不復天王作因緣。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun wept and snapped his fingers: "I only wish that in all my later lives I may never again have the karma of being Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun wept and snapped his fingers. "I only pray that in all my future lives I may never again be tied by karma to the throne."

sentences.zh: 」宮內盡哭，聲徹於外。

translations.literal: Everyone within the palace wept, and the sound reached outside.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone inside the palace wept, and the sound carried far outside.

sentences.zh: 順帝拍敬則手曰：「必無過慮，當餉輔國十萬錢。」

translations.literal: Emperor Shun patted Jingze's hand and said, "You need not worry excessively; I shall give the State-supporting Duke a hundred thousand cash."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun patted Jingze's hand and said, "You need not worry—I shall give the Duke Who Supports the State a hundred thousand cash."

sentences.zh: 二年，魏軍攻淮、泗，敬則恐，委鎮還都，百姓皆驚散奔走。

translations.literal: In the second year Wei troops attacked Huai and Si; Jingze was afraid and abandoned his command post to return to the capital, and the common people all fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Wei troops attacked the Huai and Si region. Jingze was frightened, abandoned his post, and returned to the capital, and the people fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 上以其功臣不問，以為都官尚書，遷吳興太守。

translations.literal: The emperor, because he was a meritorious minister, did not question him and appointed him Minister of Justice, then transferred him to be Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, because he was a meritorious minister, did not punish him and appointed him Minister of Justice, then transferred him to Administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 郡舊多剽掠，有十數歲小兒于路取遺物，敬則殺之以徇。

translations.literal: The commandery had long been full of plundering; a boy of ten-some years picked up lost objects on the road, and Jingze killed him as an example.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery had long been plagued by banditry. When a boy of about ten picked up something someone had dropped on the road, Jingze had him executed as a warning.

sentences.zh: 自此路不拾遺，郡無劫盜。

translations.literal: From then on nothing was left on the roads, and the commandery had no robbers.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one dared leave anything on the roads, and banditry vanished from the commandery.

sentences.zh: 又錄得一偷，召其親屬于前鞭之。

translations.literal: He also captured a thief and summoned his kin before him to flog him.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured a thief and had the man's relatives flog him in his presence.

sentences.zh: 令偷身長掃街路，久之，乃令偷舉舊偷自代。

translations.literal: He ordered the thief, who was tall, to sweep the streets; after a long while he then ordered the thief to name former thieves to replace himself.
translations.idiomatic: He made the tall thief sweep the streets. After a long while he ordered the thief to name his former accomplices to take his place.

sentences.zh: 諸偷恐為所識，皆逃走，境內以清。

translations.literal: All the thieves feared being recognized and fled; within the borders the region became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The thieves, fearing exposure, all fled, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 仍入烏程，從市過，見屠肉枅，歎曰：「吳興昔無此枅，是我少時在此所作也。

translations.literal: He then entered Wucheng and, passing through the market, saw a butcher's meat block and sighed, "Wuxing never had such a block before—it was something I made here in my youth."
translations.idiomatic: He then went into Wucheng and, passing through the market, saw a butcher's chopping block and sighed, "Wuxing never had one like this before—I made this one here when I was young."

sentences.zh: 」召故人飲酒說平生，不以屑也。

translations.literal: He summoned old friends to drink and talk of his whole life, without disdaining to do so.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned old friends to drink and reminisce about his life, unashamed of his humble past.

sentences.zh: 遷護軍，以家為府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Guardian of the Army and used his own house as his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Guardian of the Army and used his own home as his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 三年，以改葬去職，詔贈敬則母尋陽國太夫人，改授侍中、撫軍。

translations.literal: In the third year he left office to rebury his kin; an edict ennobled Jingze's mother as Grand Lady of the State of Xunyang, and he was reassigned as Palace Attendant and Pacifier of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he left office to rebury his kin. An edict ennobled Jingze's mother as Grand Lady of the State of Xunyang, and he was reassigned as Palace Attendant and Pacifier of the Army.

sentences.zh: 高帝遺詔敬則以本官領丹陽尹，尋遷會稽太守，加都督。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao's testamentary edict had Jingze retain his original office and concurrently hold the post of Intendant of Danyang; soon he was transferred to Administrator of Kuaiji with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao's testamentary edict had Jingze retain his original office and concurrently serve as Intendant of Danyang. Soon he was transferred to Administrator of Kuaiji with the added title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was granted one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was granted a full set of martial music.

sentences.zh: 會土邊帶湖海，人丁無士庶皆保塘役。

translations.literal: In Kuaiji the land bordered lakes and the sea, and every man, commoner or gentry, was liable for dike labor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kuaiji the land bordered lakes and the sea, and every man, whether commoner or gentry, was liable for dike labor.

sentences.zh: 敬則以功力有餘，悉評斂為錢送台庫，以為便宜。

translations.literal: Jingze, because there was surplus labor, assessed and collected it all as cash sent to the central treasury, regarding this as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze, finding that labor quotas left a surplus, assessed the excess as a cash levy and sent the money to the central treasury, regarding this as a practical arrangement.

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the arrangement.

sentences.zh: 三年，進號征東將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 宋廣州刺史王翼之子妾路氏酷暴，殺婢媵，翼之子法朗告之，敬則付山陰獄殺之。

translations.literal: Lu, a concubine of the son of Wang Yi, Governor of Guangzhou under Song, was cruel and violent and killed maids and secondary wives; Wang Yi's son Falang reported this, and Jingze handed her to the prison of Shanyin and had her killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu, a concubine of the son of Wang Yi, former Governor of Guangzhou under Song, was cruel and murdered maids and secondary wives. Wang Yi's son Falang reported her, and Jingze had her thrown into the Shanyin jail and executed.

sentences.zh: 路氏家訴，為有司所奏，山陰令劉岱坐棄市刑。

translations.literal: Lu's family lodged a complaint; the responsible offices memorialized the case, and Liu Dai, magistrate of Shanyin, was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Lu's family lodged a complaint. The responsible offices reported the case, and Liu Dai, magistrate of Shanyin, was sentenced to execution in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 敬則入朝，上謂敬則曰：「人命至重，是誰下意殺之？

translations.literal: When Jingze came to court the emperor said to him, "Human life is of the utmost weight—who intended that she be killed?"
translations.idiomatic: When Jingze came to court the emperor said to him, "Human life is precious—who gave the order to kill her?"

sentences.zh: 都不啟聞。

translations.literal: You never reported it at all.
translations.idiomatic: You never reported it to me at all.

sentences.zh: 」敬則曰：「是臣愚意。

translations.literal: Jingze said, "It was this subject's own foolish intent."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze said, "It was my own decision."

sentences.zh: 臣知何物科法，見背後有節，便言應得殺人。

translations.literal: This subject knows nothing of what the statutes say; seeing that behind her back she had a mole, I said she ought to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: I know nothing of the statutes. I saw she had a mole on her back and said she deserved to die.

sentences.zh: 」劉岱亦引罪，上乃赦之；

translations.literal: Liu Dai also took the blame, and the emperor then pardoned him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Dai also accepted blame, and the emperor pardoned him;

sentences.zh: 敬則免官，以公領郡。

translations.literal: Jingze was removed from office but retained the commandery as a duke.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze was stripped of office but retained the commandery in his capacity as a duke.

sentences.zh: 後與王儉俱即本號開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: Later he and Wang Jian both at once received their existing titles with the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Later he and Wang Jian were both simultaneously granted the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies while retaining their existing titles.

sentences.zh: 時徐孝嗣於崇禮門候儉，因嘲之曰：「今日可謂連璧。

translations.literal: At that time Xu Xiaosi was waiting for Jian at the Chongli Gate and jested at him, saying, "Today may truly be called paired jades."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Xu Xiaosi was waiting for Wang Jian at the Chongli Gate and teased him, saying, "Today we may truly call this a pairing of jades."

sentences.zh: 」儉曰：「不意老子遂與韓非同傳。

translations.literal: Jian said, "I never expected that this old man should share a biography with Han Fei."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian said, "I never expected that I, an old scholar, would share a biography with Han Fei."

sentences.zh: 」人以告敬則，敬則欣然曰：「我南沙縣吏，徼幸得細鎧左右，逮風雲以至於此。

translations.literal: Someone told Jingze, and he said with pleasure, "I was a clerk of Nansha County; by chance I obtained light armor at the ruler's side and, catching the wind and clouds, reached this point."
translations.idiomatic: When someone told Jingze, he said cheerfully, "I was only a clerk in Nansha County. By chance I won a place in light armor at the ruler's side and rode the winds of fortune to where I stand today."

sentences.zh: 遂與王衛軍同日拜三公，王敬則復何恨。

translations.literal: Thus on the same day as Wang the Defender of the Army I received the Three Excellencies—what regret could Wang Jingze still have?
translations.idiomatic: To receive the Three Excellencies on the same day as Wang the Defender of the Army—what more could Wang Jingze ask.

sentences.zh: 」了無恨色。

translations.literal: He showed not the least trace of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He showed not the slightest resentment.

sentences.zh: 朝士以此多之。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen for this reason admired him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The court gentlemen admired him all the more for this.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授司空。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 敬則名位雖達，不以富貴自遇。

translations.literal: Although Jingze's fame and rank had risen high, he did not treat himself as wealthy and honored.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jingze had risen to great fame and rank, he did not put on airs of wealth and privilege.

sentences.zh: 初為散輩使魏，於北館種楊柳。

translations.literal: When he first went as a member of the casual embassy to Wei, he planted a willow at the Northern Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: On his first mission to Wei as a member of the casual embassy, he planted a willow at the Northern Lodge.

sentences.zh: 後員外郎虞長曜北使還，敬則問：「我昔種楊柳樹，今若大小？

translations.literal: Later the staff member Yu Changyao returned from a northern mission, and Jingze asked, "The willow I planted in the past—how large is it now?"
translations.idiomatic: Later Yu Changyao, an outer court official, returned from a mission to the north, and Jingze asked him, "The willow I planted back then—how large is it now?"

sentences.zh: 」長曜曰：「虜中以為甘棠。

translations.literal: Changyao said, "Among the barbarians they regard it as a sweet pear tree."
translations.idiomatic: Changyao said, "Among the northerners they treat it as a sweet pear tree."

sentences.zh: 」武帝令群臣賦詩，敬則曰：「臣幾落此奴度內。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ordered the ministers to compose poems; Jingze said, "This subject nearly fell within that fellow's measure."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered the ministers to compose poems. Jingze said, "I nearly fell within that fellow's measure."

sentences.zh: 」上問之，敬則對曰：「臣若解書，不過作尚書都令史爾，那得今日。

translations.literal: The emperor asked him about this, and Jingze replied, "If this subject could read, I would be no more than a chief clerk of the Masters of Writing—how could I have reached today?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what he meant. Jingze replied, "If I could read, I would be no more than a chief clerk in the Masters of Writing—how could I have reached where I am today."

sentences.zh: 」敬則雖不大識書，而性甚警黠，臨郡令省事讀辭，下教判決，皆不失理。

translations.literal: Although Jingze did not read much, by nature he was very sharp and clever; when governing a commandery he had subordinates read documents briefly, issued instructions and judgments, and none failed to be reasonable.
translations.idiomatic: Although Jingze was barely literate, he was by nature very sharp. When governing a commandery he had subordinates summarize documents for him, issued instructions and judgments, and none failed to be sound.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，密有廢立意。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was regent he secretly had the intention of deposing the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was regent he secretly intended to depose the emperor.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年，出敬則為會稽太守，加都督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he sent Jingze out as Administrator of Kuaiji with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longchang he sent Jingze out as Administrator of Kuaiji with the added title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 海陵王立，進位太尉。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Hailing was established, Jingze was advanced to Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Hailing was enthroned, Jingze was advanced to Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，為大司馬，台使拜授日，雨大洪注，敬則文武皆失色。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne Jingze became Grand Marshal; on the day when the court envoy came to invest him with the seal, rain poured down in torrents, and all Jingze's civil and military officers turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne Jingze became Grand Marshal. On the day the court envoy came to invest him with the seal, rain poured down in torrents, and all his civil and military officers turned pale.

sentences.zh: 一客旁曰：「公由來如此，昔拜丹陽尹、吳興時亦然。

translations.literal: A guest at his side said, "My lord has always been like this; when you formerly received appointment as Intendant of Danyang and as Administrator of Wuxing it was the same."
translations.idiomatic: A guest at his side said, "My lord has always been like this—it was the same when you received appointment as Intendant of Danyang and as Administrator of Wuxing."

sentences.zh: 」敬則大悅曰：「我宿命應得雨。

translations.literal: Jingze was greatly pleased and said, "It is my destined fate to receive rain."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze was greatly pleased and said, "It is my destined fate to receive rain."

sentences.zh: 」乃引羽儀、備朝服、導引出聽事拜受，意猶不自得，吐舌久之。

translations.literal: He then brought out his guard of honor, prepared court dress, and with guides and ushers went out to the reception hall to receive the investiture; in his mind he still was not satisfied and stuck out his tongue for a long while.
translations.idiomatic: He then brought out his guard of honor, put on court dress, and with guides and ushers went out to the reception hall to receive the investiture. In his mind he still felt uneasy and stuck out his tongue for a long while.

sentences.zh: 帝既多殺害，敬則自以高、武舊臣，心懷憂懼。

translations.literal: Since the emperor had killed many people, Jingze, considering himself an old minister of Gao and Wu, harbored worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor had killed so many people, Jingze, as an old minister of the Gao and Wu emperors, lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 帝雖外厚其禮而內相疑備，數訪問敬則飲食體幹。

translations.literal: Although outwardly the emperor treated him with generous ceremony, inwardly he was suspicious and on guard, repeatedly inquiring about Jingze's food and bodily condition.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly the emperor treated him with generous ceremony, but inwardly he was suspicious and on guard, repeatedly inquiring about Jingze's diet and health.

sentences.zh: 聞其衰老，且以居內地，故得少安。

translations.literal: Hearing that he was aged and moreover that he dwelt in the interior, the emperor therefore felt somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that he was aged and that he lived in the interior, the emperor felt somewhat reassured.

sentences.zh: 後遣蕭坦之將齋仗五百人行晉陵，敬則諸子在都，憂怖無計。

translations.literal: Later he sent Xiao Tanzhi leading five hundred ceremonial guards to proceed to Jinling; Jingze's sons were all in the capital and were anxious and terrified without any plan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sent Xiao Tanzhi with five hundred ceremonial guards to Jinling. Jingze's sons were all in the capital and were terrified, with no idea what to do.

sentences.zh: 上知之，問計于梁武帝，武帝曰：「敬則豎夫，易為感，唯應錫以子女玉帛，厚其使人，如斯而已。

translations.literal: The emperor knew of this and asked Emperor Wu of Liang for a plan; Emperor Wu said, "Jingze is a common fellow, easy to move by feeling; one should only bestow on him children, jade, and silks, and treat his envoys generously—nothing more than this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor learned of this and asked Emperor Wu of Liang for advice. Emperor Wu said, "Jingze is a common soldier at heart, easy to sway. You need only bestow children, jade, and silks on him and treat his envoys generously—nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」上納之。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted this advice.

sentences.zh: 吳人張思祖，敬則謀主也，為府司馬，頻銜使。

translations.literal: Zhang Sizu of Wu, Jingze's chief strategist, served as headquarters marshal and frequently went as envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sizu of Wu, Jingze's chief strategist, served as headquarters marshal and was frequently sent as envoy.

sentences.zh: 上偽傾意待之，以為遊擊將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor pretended to treat him with full favor and appointed him General of Roaming Attack.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor pretended to treat him with full favor and appointed him General of Roaming Attack.

sentences.zh: 遣敬則世子仲雄入東。

translations.literal: He sent Jingze's heir Zhongxiong into the east.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Jingze's heir Zhongxiong to the eastern capital.

sentences.zh: 仲雄善彈琴，江左有蔡邕焦尾琴在主衣庫，上敕五日一給仲雄。

translations.literal: Zhongxiong was skilled at the zither; south of the Yangzi there was Cai Yong's Scorch-Tail zither in the imperial wardrobe store, and the emperor ordered that it be lent to Zhongxiong once every five days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiong was skilled at the zither. Cai Yong's famous Scorch-Tail zither was kept in the imperial wardrobe, and the emperor ordered that it be lent to Zhongxiong once every five days.

sentences.zh: 仲雄在御前鼓琴，作懊儂曲，歌曰：「常歎負情儂，郎今果行許。

translations.literal: Zhongxiong played the zither before the emperor, composed the Melancholy Nong tune, and sang, "I always lament the faithless lover—my lord has now truly gone so far."
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxiong played before the emperor, performing the Melancholy Nong tune and singing, "I always lament a faithless lover—my lord has now truly gone so far."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「君行不淨心，那得惡人題。

translations.literal: He also sang, "If your heart is not pure in going, how can you bear the inscription of a wicked man?"
translations.idiomatic: He also sang, "If your heart is not pure in what you do, how can you bear the mark of a wicked man?"

sentences.zh: 」帝愈猜愧。

translations.literal: The emperor grew all the more suspicious and ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew ever more suspicious and ashamed.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，帝疾屢經危殆，以張瑰為平東將軍、吳郡太守，置兵佐，密防敬則。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor's illness repeatedly reached critical danger; he appointed Zhang Gui General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wu commandery, stationed military aides, and secretly guarded against Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai the emperor's illness repeatedly turned critical. He appointed Zhang Gui General Who Pacifies the East and Administrator of Wu commandery, stationed military aides, and secretly guarded against Jingze.

sentences.zh: 內外傳言當有處分。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the court rumors spread that action would be taken against him.
translations.idiomatic: Inside and outside the court rumors spread that he was about to be dealt with.

sentences.zh: 敬則聞之，竊曰：「東今有誰，只是欲平我耳。

translations.literal: Jingze heard this and said privately, "Who is there in the east now? They only want to pacify me."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze heard this and muttered, "Who is there in the east now? They only want to get rid of me."

sentences.zh: 東亦何易可平，吾終不受金罌。

translations.literal: The east is not so easily pacified; I will never accept the golden goblet.
translations.idiomatic: The east is not so easily pacified, and I will never accept the golden goblet.

sentences.zh: 」金罌謂鴆酒也。

translations.literal: The golden goblet means poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: The golden goblet meant poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 諸子怖懼，第五子幼隆遣正員將軍徐岳以情告徐州行事謝朓為計，若同者當往報敬則。

translations.literal: His sons were terrified; the fifth son Youlong sent the regular general Xu Yue to tell Xie Tiao, who was acting for Xuzhou, the full situation and seek a plan—if he agreed he would go report to Jingze.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were terrified. His fifth son Youlong sent Regular General Xu Yue to confide in Xie Tiao, who was acting for Xuzhou, and ask his advice—if Xie Tiao agreed, he would report back to Jingze.

sentences.zh: 朓執嶽馳啟之。

translations.literal: Tiao seized Yue and galloped to report this.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Tiao seized Xu Yue and galloped to report the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 敬則城局參軍徐庶家在京口，其子密以報庶，庶以告敬則五官王公林。

translations.literal: Jingze's headquarters aide Xu Shu had his family in Jingkou; his son secretly reported this to Shu, and Shu told Jingze's aide of the Five Offices Wang Gonglin.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's headquarters aide Xu Shu had family in Jingkou. Shu's son secretly reported the news to him, and Shu told Jingze's aide of the Five Offices Wang Gonglin.

sentences.zh: 公林，敬則族子也，常所委信。

translations.literal: Gonglin was Jingze's clansman and one in whom he always placed trust.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin was Jingze's clansman and one of his most trusted men.

sentences.zh: 公林勸敬則急送啟賜兒死，單舟星夜還都。

translations.literal: Gonglin urged Jingze urgently to send a memorial asking that his son be granted death and to return to the capital alone in a boat by starlight.
translations.idiomatic: Gonglin urged Jingze to send an urgent memorial asking that his son be put to death and to return to the capital alone that very night by boat.

sentences.zh: 敬則曰：「若爾，諸郎要應有信，且忍一夕。

translations.literal: Jingze said, "If so, the young lords ought to have sent word; let us endure one night."
translations.idiomatic: Jingze said, "If that were so, my sons ought to have sent word. Let us wait one night."

sentences.zh: 」其夜，呼僚佐文武摴蒱賭錢，謂眾曰：「卿諸人欲令我作何計？

translations.literal: That night he summoned his civil and military subordinates to play pitch-pot and gamble for cash, and said to the assembly, "You all—what plan do you want me to make?"
translations.idiomatic: That night he summoned his civil and military staff to play pitch-pot and gamble, and asked the assembly, "What do you want me to do?"

sentences.zh: 」莫敢先答。

translations.literal: No one dared answer first.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared answer first.

sentences.zh: 防合丁興懷曰：「官只應作爾。

translations.literal: The guard commander Ding Xinghuai said, "My lord should only do this."
translations.idiomatic: Guard commander Ding Xinghuai said, "My lord should do just that."

sentences.zh: 」敬則不作聲。

translations.literal: Jingze made no sound.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze said nothing.

sentences.zh: 明旦，召山陰令王詢、台傳御史鍾離祖願，敬則橫刀跂坐，問詢等發丁可得幾人，庫見有幾錢物，詢、祖願對並乖旨，敬則怒，將出斬之。

translations.literal: At dawn the next day he summoned the magistrate of Shanyin Wang Xun and the investigating censor Zhongli Zuyuan; Jingze sat with sword across his knees and asked Xun and the others how many men could be mobilized and how much cash was in the treasury—Xun and Zuyuan answered contrary to his intent, Jingze was angry, and was about to take them out and behead them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the next day he summoned the magistrate of Shanyin Wang Xun and investigating censor Zhongli Zuyuan. Jingze sat with his sword across his knees and asked how many men could be mobilized and how much cash was in the treasury. Wang Xun and Zhongli Zuyuan gave answers he did not want to hear. Jingze flew into a rage and was about to have them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 王公林又諫敬則曰：「官詎不更思？

translations.literal: Wang Gonglin again remonstrated with Jingze, saying, "My lord, will you not reconsider?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gonglin again remonstrated with him, saying, "My lord, will you not reconsider?"

sentences.zh: 」敬則唾其面，曰：「小子，我作事何關汝小子。

translations.literal: Jingze spat in his face and said, "Boy—what does my doing things have to do with you, boy?"
translations.idiomatic: Jingze spat in his face and said, "Boy—what does my business have to do with you?"

sentences.zh: 」乃起兵，招集配衣，二三日便發。

translations.literal: He then raised troops, gathered men under his banner, and set out within two or three days.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised troops, gathered his followers, and set out within two or three days.

sentences.zh: 欲劫前中書令何胤還為尚書令，長史王弄璋、司馬張思祖止之曰：「何令高蹈，必不從，不從便應殺之。

translations.literal: He wished to seize the former Secretariat Director He Yin and restore him as Director of the Masters of Writing; the chief administrator Wang Nongzhang and headquarters marshal Zhang Sizu stopped him, saying, "Director He lives in lofty seclusion and will certainly not follow; if he does not follow he ought to be killed."
translations.idiomatic: He planned to seize former Secretariat Director He Yin and make him Director of the Masters of Writing again. Chief administrator Wang Nongzhang and headquarters marshal Zhang Sizu stopped him, saying, "Director He lives in lofty seclusion and will never go along. If he refuses, you would have to kill him."

sentences.zh: 舉大事先殺朝賢，事必不濟。

translations.literal: To raise a great affair and first kill court worthies—the affair will certainly not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: To launch a great enterprise by first killing court worthies—the affair will certainly fail.

sentences.zh: 」乃率實甲萬人過浙江，謂曰：「應須作檄。

translations.literal: He then led ten thousand men in solid armor across the Zhe River and said, "We ought to draw up a proclamation."
translations.idiomatic: He then led ten thousand armored men across the Zhe River and said, "We ought to issue a proclamation."

sentences.zh: 」思祖曰：「公今自還朝，何用作此？

translations.literal: Sizu said, "My lord is now returning to court himself—why make this?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Sizu said, "You are returning to court yourself—why bother with that?"

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: He then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He dropped the idea.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣輔國將軍前軍司馬左興盛、直合將軍馬軍主胡松三千餘人，築壘于曲阿長岡；

translations.literal: The court sent the Pacifying-the-State general and former army marshal Zuo Xingsheng and the direct-gate general and cavalry commander Hu Song with more than three thousand men to build fortifications at Changgang in Qu'a;
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Pacifying-the-State general and former army marshal Zuo Xingsheng and direct-gate general and cavalry commander Hu Song with more than three thousand men to build fortifications at Changgang in Qu'a;

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射沈文秀為持節、都督，屯湖頭，備京口路。

translations.literal: the Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenxiu was made bearer of the staff of authority and area commander, encamped at Hutou, and guarded the route to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Shen Wenxiu was made bearer of the staff of authority and area commander, encamped at Hutou to guard the route to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 敬則以舊將舉事，百姓擔篙荷鍤隨逐之十餘萬眾。

translations.literal: Jingze, as an old general raising the affair, was followed by more than a hundred thousand common people carrying poles and shouldering spades.
translations.idiomatic: As an old general raising a revolt, Jingze was followed by more than a hundred thousand common people carrying poles and spades.

sentences.zh: 至武進陵口慟哭，乘肩輿而前。

translations.literal: When he reached the mouth of the Wujin imperial tombs he wept bitterly and rode forward in a shoulder-borne carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached the mouth of the Wujin imperial tombs he wept bitterly and was carried forward in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 遇興盛、山陽二柴，盡力攻之。

translations.literal: He encountered the two palisades of Xingsheng and Shanyang and attacked them with all his strength.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the two palisades of Xingsheng and Shanyang and attacked them with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 官軍不敵，欲退而圍不開，各死戰。

translations.literal: The government troops could not match them and wished to retreat, but the encirclement would not open, and each side fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops could not hold and tried to retreat, but the encirclement would not break, and both sides fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 胡松領馬軍突其後，白丁無器仗，皆驚散。

translations.literal: Hu Song led the cavalry in a thrust at their rear; the common levies had no weapons or armor and all fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Song led the cavalry in a charge at their rear. The common levies had no weapons or armor and fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 敬則大叫索馬，再上不得上，興盛軍容袁文曠斬之傳首。

translations.literal: Jingze shouted loudly for a horse but could not mount again; Yuan Wenkuan, aide to Xingsheng's army, cut him down and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze shouted for a horse but could not mount again. Yuan Wenkuan, aide to Xingsheng's army, cut him down and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 是時上疾已篤，敬則倉卒東起，朝廷震懼。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor's illness was already grave; Jingze had hastily risen in the east, and the court was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor's illness was grave. Jingze had risen hastily in the east, and the court was shaken with fear.

sentences.zh: 東昏侯在東宮議欲叛，使人上屋望，見征虜亭失火，謂敬則至，急裝欲走。

translations.literal: Marquis of Donghun in the Eastern Palace discussed rebelling; he sent someone up on the roof to look, saw the Zheng Lu Pavilion catch fire, thought Jingze had arrived, and hurriedly packed to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Donghun in the Eastern Palace discussed rebelling. He sent someone onto the roof to look out, saw the Zheng Lu Pavilion catch fire, thought Jingze had arrived, and hurriedly packed to flee.

sentences.zh: 有告敬則者，敬則曰：「檀公三十六策，走是上計，汝父子唯應急走耳。

translations.literal: Someone reported this to Jingze, and Jingze said, "Lord Tan's thirty-six stratagems—flight is the best plan; you father and son ought only to flee in haste."
translations.idiomatic: When someone reported this to Jingze, he said, "Lord Tan's thirty-six stratagems—running away is the best plan. You father and son ought to flee at once."

sentences.zh: 」蓋譏檀道濟避魏事也。

translations.literal: This mocked Tan Daoji's affair of avoiding Wei.
translations.idiomatic: This mocked Tan Daoji's flight from the Wei.

sentences.zh: 敬則之來，聲勢甚盛，凡十日而敗。

translations.literal: Jingze's coming had a very grand momentum, yet within ten days he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze's revolt had seemed overwhelmingly powerful, yet within ten days it was crushed.

sentences.zh: 時年六十四。

translations.literal: He was then sixty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 朝廷漆其首藏在武庫，至梁天監元年，其故吏夏侯亶表請收葬，許之。

translations.literal: The court lacquered his head and stored it in the armory; down to the first year of Tianjian under Liang, his former clerk Xia Hou Dan memorialized requesting burial, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court lacquered his head and stored it in the armory. In the first year of Tianjian under Liang, his former clerk Xia Hou Dan memorialized requesting burial, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 陳顯達

translations.literal: Chen Xianda
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda

sentences.zh: 陳顯達，南彭城彭城人也。

translations.literal: Chen Xianda was a native of Pengcheng in Southern Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xianda was a native of Pengcheng in Southern Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 仕宋以軍功封彭澤縣子，位羽林監、濮陽太守，隸齊高帝討桂陽賊於新亭壘。

translations.literal: He served Song and for military merit was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pengze County, held the posts of Feathered Forest commandant and Administrator of Puyang, and was attached to Emperor Gao of Qi in attacking the Guiyang rebels at the Xinting ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Song and for military merit was enfeoffed as Viscount of Pengze County. He held the posts of Feathered Forest commandant and Administrator of Puyang and served under Emperor Gao of Qi against the Guiyang rebels at the Xinting ramparts.

sentences.zh: 劉勉大桁敗，賊進杜姥宅。

translations.literal: Liu Mian was greatly defeated at the Great Beam, and the rebels advanced to the Old Woman Du's residence.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mian was routed at the Great Beam, and the rebels advanced to the Old Woman Du's residence.

sentences.zh: 及休范死，顯達出杜姥宅，大戰于宣陽津陽門，大破賊，矢中左目而鏃不出。

translations.literal: When Xiu Fan died, Xianda came out of the Old Woman Du's residence and fought a great battle at the Xuanyang Ford Yang Gate, greatly defeating the rebels; an arrow struck his left eye and the head would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu Fan died, Xianda came out of the Old Woman Du's residence and fought a great battle at the Xuanyang Ford Yang Gate, routing the rebels. An arrow struck his left eye and the arrowhead would not come out.

sentences.zh: 地黃村潘嫗善禁，先以釘釘柱，嫗禹步作氣，釘即出，乃禁顯達目中鏃出之。

translations.literal: The old woman Pan of Dihuang village was skilled at exorcism; first a nail was driven into a pillar, the old woman paced in Yu's steps and made breath, the nail came out at once, and then she exorcised the arrowhead out of Xianda's eye.
translations.idiomatic: Old woman Pan of Dihuang village was skilled at exorcism. First a nail was driven into a pillar; she paced in ritual steps and made breath, the nail came out at once, and then she exorcised the arrowhead out of Xianda's eye.

sentences.zh: 事平，封豐城侯，再遷平越中郎將、廣州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng, then was transferred again to General of the Gentlemen of the Household for Pacifying the Yue and Administrator of Guangzhou, with the added title of Area Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was restored he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengcheng, then was transferred to General of the Gentlemen of the Household for Pacifying the Yue and Administrator of Guangzhou, with the added title of Area Commander.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，進號鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne his title was advanced to General Who Guards the West.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne his title was advanced to General Who Guards the West.

sentences.zh: 益部山險，多不賓服。

translations.literal: The mountains of Yizhou were perilous, and many did not submit in guest-like obedience.
translations.idiomatic: The mountains of Yizhou were rugged, and many tribes did not submit.

sentences.zh: 大度村獠，前刺史不能制，顯達遣使責其租賧。

translations.literal: The Liao of Dadu village—former governors could not control them; Xianda sent envoys to demand their rent and tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao of Dadu village had defied previous governors. Xianda sent envoys to demand their rent and tribute.

sentences.zh: 獠帥曰：「兩眼刺史尚不敢調我。

translations.literal: The Liao chief said, "Even the two-eyed governor did not dare press me."
translations.idiomatic: The Liao chief said, "Even the two-eyed governor did not dare press me."

sentences.zh: 」遂殺其使。

translations.literal: He then killed the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He then killed the envoy.

sentences.zh: 顯達分部將吏，聲將出獵，夜往襲之，男女無少長皆斬之。

translations.literal: Xianda divided his officers and clerks, gave out that he would go hunting, went by night to attack them, and beheaded men and women without regard to age.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda divided his officers, announced that he would go hunting, attacked them by night, and beheaded men and women without regard to age.

sentences.zh: 自此山夷震服。

translations.literal: From then on the mountain tribes were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the mountain tribes submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，徵為侍中、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming he was summoned as Palace Attendant and Guardian of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming he was summoned to serve as Palace Attendant and Guardian of the Army.

sentences.zh: 顯達累任在外，經高帝之憂。

translations.literal: Xianda had repeatedly served outside the capital and had passed through Emperor Gao's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda had long served in the provinces and had been away during Emperor Gao's final illness.

sentences.zh: 及見武帝，流涕悲咽，上亦泣，心甚嘉之。

translations.literal: When he saw Emperor Wu he wept and sobbed with grief; the emperor also wept and in his heart greatly prized him.
translations.idiomatic: When he saw Emperor Wu he wept aloud. The emperor wept as well and was deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 八年，為征南大將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he became Grand General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he became Grand General Who Campaigns South and Inspector of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯達謙厚有智計，自以人微位重，每遷官常有愧懼之色。

translations.literal: Xianda was modest, generous, and possessed of stratagems; considering himself a man of slight standing in a weighty post, whenever he was transferred he often showed a look of shame and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda was modest, thoughtful, and shrewd. Considering himself a man of humble origin in a weighty post, he often looked ashamed and uneasy whenever he was promoted.

sentences.zh: 子十餘人，誡之曰：「我本意不及此，汝等勿以富貴陵人。

translations.literal: He had more than ten sons and admonished them, saying, "My original intent did not reach this far—you must not use wealth and honor to bully others."
translations.idiomatic: He had more than ten sons and admonished them, saying, "I never intended to rise this high—you must not use wealth and rank to bully others."

sentences.zh: 」家既豪富，諸子與王敬則諸兒並精車牛，麗服飾。

translations.literal: The family was already wealthy and powerful; his sons and the sons of Wang Jingze alike had fine chariots and oxen and splendid dress.
translations.idiomatic: His family was already wealthy, and his sons, like the sons of Wang Jingze, kept fine chariots and oxen and dressed lavishly.

sentences.zh: 當世快牛稱陳世子青、王三郎烏、呂文顯折角、江瞿曇白鼻，而皆集陳舍。

translations.literal: The fast oxen of the age were called Chen the Heir's Green, Wang the Third Son's Black, Lü Wenxian's Bent Horn, and Jiang Qudan's White Nose, and all were gathered at Chen's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The finest oxen of the day were known as Chen the Heir's Green, Wang the Third Son's Black, Lü Wenxian's Bent Horn, and Jiang Qudan's White Nose, and all were kept at Chen's residence.

sentences.zh: 顯達知此不悅。

translations.literal: Xianda knew of this and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda knew of this and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 及子休尚為郢府主簿，過九江拜別。

translations.literal: When his son Xiushang was chief clerk of the Ying headquarters and passed through Jiujiang to take leave,
translations.idiomatic: When his son Xiushang, chief clerk of the Ying headquarters, passed through Jiujiang to take leave,

sentences.zh: 顯達曰：「凡奢侈者鮮有不敗，麈尾蠅拂是王、謝家物，汝不須捉此自逐。

translations.literal: Xianda said, "All who are extravagant rarely escape ruin; deer-tail and fly-whisk are things of the Wang and Xie families—you need not grasp these to pursue yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Xianda said to him, "The extravagant rarely escape ruin. Deer-tail and fly-whisk fans are the trappings of the Wang and Xie families—you need not chase after such things."

sentences.zh: 」即取於前燒除之。

translations.literal: He immediately took them before him and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately took them and burned them before him.

sentences.zh: 其靜退如此。

translations.literal: His quiet withdrawal was like this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his restraint.

sentences.zh: 豫廢郁林之勳，延興元年，為司空，進爵為公。

translations.literal: For his merit in the deposition of Prince of Yulin, in the first year of Yanxing he became Minister of Works and his noble rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit in deposing the Prince of Yulin, in the first year of Yanxing he was appointed Minister of Works and advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 明帝即位，進太尉，封鄱陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was advanced to Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Duke of Poyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne he was advanced to Grand Commandant and enfeoffed as Duke of Poyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 加兵二百人，給油絡車。

translations.literal: Two hundred soldiers were added to his guard, and he was given an oil-lacquered carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred soldiers were added to his guard, and he was given an oil-lacquered carriage.

sentences.zh: 後以太尉封鄱陽郡公，為三公事，而職典連率，人以為格外三公。

translations.literal: Later, as Grand Commandant enfeoffed as Duke of Poyang commandery, he held the affairs of the Three Excellencies yet his office was that of a regional inspector, and people regarded him as a Three Excellency beyond the norm.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Grand Commandant and Duke of Poyang commandery, he held the rank of the Three Excellencies while also serving as regional inspector, and people regarded him as a Three Excellency beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 上欲悉除高、武子孫，上微言問顯達，答曰：「此等豈足介慮。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to eliminate all the descendants of Gao and Wu; he spoke subtly and asked Xianda, who answered, "Such people are hardly worth troubling over."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to eliminate all the descendants of the Gao and Wu emperors. He spoke subtly to Xianda, who answered, "Such people are hardly worth troubling over."

sentences.zh: 」上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 顯達建武世心懷不安，深自貶退，車乘朽敗，導從鹵簿皆用羸小。

translations.literal: In the Jianwu era Xianda harbored unease in his heart, deeply lowered himself, his carriages and mounts were rotten and broken, and his guides and ceremonial guard all used weak and small men.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era Xianda lived in unease, deliberately lowered his profile, used broken-down carriages, and kept only weak, undersized men in his escort and ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 侍宴，酒後啟上借枕，帝令與之。

translations.literal: At a banquet he waited on the emperor; after wine he requested to borrow a pillow, and the emperor ordered that one be given him.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet, after drinking he asked the emperor to lend him a pillow, and the emperor had one given to him.

sentences.zh: 顯達撫枕曰：「臣年已老，富貴已足，唯少枕枕死，特就陛下乞之。

translations.literal: Xianda stroked the pillow and said, "This subject is already old, wealth and honor are enough—only a pillow on which to die is lacking; I specially come before Your Majesty to beg it."
translations.idiomatic: Xianda stroked the pillow and said, "I am already old and have had wealth and honor enough. I lack only a pillow on which to die, and I come before Your Majesty specially to beg it."

sentences.zh: 」上失色曰：「公醉矣。

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and said, "My lord is drunk."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned pale and said, "You are drunk."

sentences.zh: 」以年老告退，不許。

translations.literal: He reported his wish to retire on grounds of age, but this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to retire on grounds of age, but permission was refused.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年，乃遣顯達北侵。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongtai he then sent Xianda to invade the north.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongtai he sent Xianda to invade the north.

sentences.zh: 永元元年，顯達督平北將軍崔慧景眾軍四萬圍南鄉界馬圈城，去襄陽三百里。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongyuan Xianda supervised the armies of the four myriad men under the Pacifying-the-North general Cui Huijing in besieging the Horse-Pen city on the border of Nanxiang, three hundred li from Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongyuan Xianda supervised an army of forty thousand men under Pacifying-the-North general Cui Huijing in besieging Horse-Pen city on the Nanxiang border, three hundred li from Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 攻之四十日，魏軍食盡，噉死人肉及樹皮。

translations.literal: They attacked for forty days; the Wei army's food was exhausted and they ate the flesh of the dead and tree bark.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted forty days. The Wei army ran out of food and ate the flesh of the dead and tree bark.

sentences.zh: 周邊急，魏軍突走。

translations.literal: The encirclement was pressing and the Wei army broke out and fled.
translations.idiomatic: With the encirclement pressing in, the Wei army broke out and fled.

sentences.zh: 顯達入據其城，遣軍主莊丘黑進取南鄉縣。

translations.literal: Xianda entered and occupied the city, and sent the army commander Zhuangqiu Hei to seize Nanxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda entered and occupied the city and sent army commander Zhuangqiu Hei to seize Nanxiang county.

sentences.zh: 魏孝文帝自領十餘萬騎奄至，軍主崔恭祖、胡松以烏布幔盛顯達，數人擔之，出汮水口，台軍緣道奔退，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei himself led more than a hundred thousand horsemen and came upon them suddenly; the army commanders Cui Gongzu and Hu Song wrapped Xianda in a black-cloth canopy and several men carried him out at the Fenshui mouth—the court army fled along the road in retreat, and more than thirty thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen of Wei himself led more than a hundred thousand horsemen and came upon them suddenly. Army commanders Cui Gongzu and Hu Song wrapped Xianda in a black-cloth canopy and several men carried him out at the Fenshui mouth. The court army fled along the road, and more than thirty thousand men died.

sentences.zh: 顯達素有威名，著於外境，至是大損喪焉。

translations.literal: Xianda had long had a reputation for authority established on the outer borders; on this occasion he suffered great loss.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda had long enjoyed a formidable reputation on the frontier, but on this occasion he suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞範岫奏免顯達官，又表解職，並不許。

translations.literal: The investigating censor Fan Xiu memorialized to remove Xianda from office, and Xianda also submitted a memorial resigning his post—neither was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Fan Xiu memorialized to strip Xianda of office, and Xianda also submitted a resignation—both were refused.

sentences.zh: 以為江州刺史，鎮盆城。

translations.literal: He was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou and garrisoned Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Inspector of Jiangzhou and garrisoned Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 初，王敬則事起，始安王遙光啟明帝慮顯達為變，欲追軍還，事平乃寢。

translations.literal: At first, when Wang Jingze's affair arose, the Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang reported to Emperor Ming that he feared Xianda might change sides and wished to recall the army; when the affair was settled this was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jingze's revolt broke out, the Prince of Shi'an Yao Guang warned Emperor Ming that Xianda might turn against the court and urged that the army be recalled. When the revolt was crushed the idea was dropped.

sentences.zh: 顯達亦懷危怖。

translations.literal: Xianda also harbored fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda also lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 及東昏立，彌不樂還都，得此授甚喜。

translations.literal: When Donghun was established he was all the less willing to return to the capital; receiving this appointment he was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun was enthroned he was even less willing to return to the capital and was very pleased to receive this appointment.

sentences.zh: 尋加領征南大將軍，給三望車。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made concurrent Grand General Who Campaigns South and given a three-canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was additionally made concurrent Grand General Who Campaigns South and given a three-canopy carriage.

sentences.zh: 顯達聞都下大相殺戮，徐孝嗣等皆死，傳聞當遣兵襲江州。

translations.literal: Xianda heard that in the capital there was great mutual slaughter and that Xu Xiaosi and others had all died; rumors spread that troops would be sent to attack Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda heard that the capital was engulfed in slaughter and that Xu Xiaosi and others had all been killed. Rumors spread that troops would be sent to attack Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯達懼禍，十一月十五日舉兵，欲直襲建鄴，以掩不備，又遙指郢州刺史建安王寶寅為主。

translations.literal: Xianda feared disaster; on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month he raised troops, wishing to strike Jianye directly to take them unawares, and also pointed from afar to the Inspector of Yingzhou, the Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, as his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for his life, on the fifteenth day of the eleventh month Xianda raised troops, intending to strike Jianye directly and catch the court off guard, while nominating the Inspector of Yingzhou, the Prince of Jian'an Bao Yin, as his sovereign.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣後軍將軍胡松等據梁山，顯達率眾數千人發尋陽，與松戰於採石，大破之，都下震恐。

translations.literal: The court sent the Rear Army general Hu Song and others to hold Liangshan; Xianda led several thousand men setting out from Xunyang, fought Song at Caishi, greatly defeated him, and the capital was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Rear Army general Hu Song and others to hold Liangshan. Xianda led several thousand men from Xunyang, fought Hu Song at Caishi, routed him, and threw the capital into terror.

sentences.zh: 十二月，潛軍度取石頭北上襲城，宮掖大駭，閉門守備。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he secretly sent troops across to seize Shitou and advance north to assault the city; the palace quarters were greatly terrified and closed the gates to defend.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he secretly sent troops across the river to seize Shitou and advance north to assault the city. The palace was thrown into panic and closed its gates to defend.

sentences.zh: 顯達馬睄從步軍數百人，於西州前與台軍戰，再合大勝，綃折，手猶殺十餘人。

translations.literal: Xianda, with bloodshot eyes, followed several hundred infantry; before the Western Quarter he fought the court army, twice joined battle and won great victories, his silk armor was broken, yet by hand he still killed more than ten men.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda, his eyes bloodshot, followed several hundred infantry. Before the Western Quarter he fought the court army, won two great victories in succession, had his silk armor cut through, and still killed more than ten men with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 官軍繼至，顯達不能抗，退走至西州後烏榜村。

translations.literal: Government troops continued to arrive; Xianda could not resist and retreated to Wubang village behind the Western Quarter.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops kept arriving. Xianda could not hold and retreated to Wubang village behind the Western Quarter.

sentences.zh: 騎官趙潭注綃刺落馬，斬之籬側，血湧湔籬，似淳于伯之被刑。

translations.literal: The cavalry officer Zhao Tan drove his blade through the silk armor and knocked him from his horse, beheaded him beside a hedge, blood gushed and splashed the hedge, like Chunyu Bo undergoing execution.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry officer Zhao Tan drove his blade through Xianda's silk armor and knocked him from his horse, then beheaded him beside a hedge. Blood gushed and splashed the hedge, recalling the execution of Chunyu Bo.

sentences.zh: 時年七十三。

translations.literal: He was then seventy-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-three years old.

sentences.zh: 顯達在江州遇疾，不療之而差，意甚不悅。

translations.literal: Xianda fell ill in Jiangzhou, recovered without treatment, and was very displeased in his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Xianda fell ill in Jiangzhou and recovered without treatment, which displeased him greatly.

sentences.zh: 是時連冬大雪，梟首朱雀而雪不集，諸子皆伏誅。

translations.literal: At that time snow fell continuously through the winter; his head was displayed at the Vermilion Bird gate yet snow would not settle on it, and all his sons were executed.
translations.idiomatic: That winter snow fell continuously. His head was displayed at the Vermilion Bird gate, yet snow would not settle on it, and all his sons were executed.

sentences.zh: 張敬兒

translations.literal: Zhang Jing'er
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing'er

sentences.zh: 張敬兒，南陽冠軍人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jing'er was a native of Guanjun in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jing'er was a native of Guanjun in Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 父醜，為郡將軍，官至節府參軍。

translations.literal: His father Chou was a commandery general and reached the post of headquarters aide.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chou was a commandery general and rose to headquarters aide.

sentences.zh: 敬兒年少便弓馬、有膽氣，好射猛獸，發無不中。

translations.literal: Jing'er from youth was skilled in bow and horse and possessed courage, fond of shooting fierce beasts—every shot hit.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jing'er was skilled with bow and horse and full of courage. He loved hunting fierce beasts and never missed his mark.

sentences.zh: 南陽新野風俗出騎射，而敬兒尤多膂力。

translations.literal: The custom of Xinye in Nanyang produced horsemen and archers, but Jing'er had especially great physical strength.
translations.idiomatic: Xinye in Nanyang was known for producing horsemen and archers, but Jing'er had exceptional physical strength.

sentences.zh: 稍官至寧蠻行參軍，隨郡人劉胡伐襄陽諸山蠻，深入險阻，所向皆破。

translations.literal: He gradually reached the post of acting aide for Pacifying the Barbarians and followed Liu Hu of Suizhou in attacking the mountain tribes around Xiangyang; penetrating deep into perilous terrain, wherever he went he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually rose to acting aide for Pacifying the Barbarians and followed Liu Hu of Suizhou in attacking the mountain tribes around Xiangyang. Penetrating deep into rugged terrain, he broke every force he met.

sentences.zh: 又擊胡陽蠻，官軍引退，敬兒單馬在後，賊不能抗。

translations.literal: He also attacked the Huyang tribes; the government army withdrew, Jing'er alone on horseback in the rear, and the rebels could not withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the Huyang tribes. When the government army withdrew, Jing'er alone on horseback brought up the rear, and the rebels could not stand against him.

sentences.zh: 山陽王休佑鎮壽陽，求善騎射士，敬兒及襄陽俞湛應選。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou garrisoned Shouyang and sought skilled horsemen and archers; Jing'er and Yu Zhan of Xiangyang were selected.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shanyang Xiuyou garrisoned Shouyang and sought skilled horsemen and archers. Jing'er and Yu Zhan of Xiangyang were selected.

sentences.zh: 敬兒善事人，遂見寵，為長兼行參軍。

translations.literal: Jing'er was good at serving people and thus won favor, becoming chief acting aide.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er knew how to please his superiors and won favor, becoming chief acting aide.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，隨府轉驃騎參軍，署中兵，領軍討義嘉賊，與劉胡相拒於鵲尾洲，啟明帝乞本郡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he followed the headquarters and was transferred to Rapid-as-Leopards aide, acting as central army commander, leading the army to attack the Yijia rebels, and faced Liu Hu at Magpie-Tail Islet; he reported to Emperor Ming requesting his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi he was transferred to Rapid-as-Leopards aide and acted as central army commander, leading troops against the Yijia rebels and facing Liu Hu at Magpie-Tail Islet. He memorialized Emperor Ming requesting his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 事平，除南陽太守。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he was appointed Administrator of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: When peace was restored he was appointed Administrator of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 敬兒之為襄陽府將也，家貧，每休假輒傭賃自給。

translations.literal: When Jing'er was a headquarters general at Xiangyang his family was poor, and whenever he had leave he hired himself out for wages to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing'er was a headquarters general at Xiangyang his family was poor, and on every leave he hired himself out for wages to make ends meet.

sentences.zh: 嘗為城東吳泰家擔水，通泰所愛婢。

translations.literal: He once carried water for Wu Tai east of the city and had an affair with Tai's favorite maid.
translations.idiomatic: He once carried water for Wu Tai east of the city and had an affair with Tai's favorite maid.

sentences.zh: 事發，將被泰殺，逃賣棺材中，以蓋加上，乃免。

translations.literal: When the affair came out he was about to be killed by Tai; he fled and hid in a coffin being sold, had the lid placed on top, and thus escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was discovered he was about to be killed by Tai. He fled and hid inside a coffin for sale, had the lid placed on top, and thus escaped.

sentences.zh: 及在鵲尾洲，啟明帝云：「泰以絲助雍州刺史袁顗為弩弦，黨同為逆，若事平之日，乞其家財。

translations.literal: When at Magpie-Tail Islet he reported to Emperor Ming, "Tai used silk to help Yuan Yi, Governor of Yongzhou, make crossbow strings; he was a partisan in rebellion—if the day of peace comes, I beg his family property."
translations.idiomatic: At Magpie-Tail Islet he reported to Emperor Ming, "Tai supplied silk to Yuan Yi, Governor of Yongzhou, for crossbow strings. He was a partisan in rebellion—when peace is restored, I ask for his family property."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted the request.

sentences.zh: 至是收籍吳氏，唯家人裸身得出，僮役財貨直數千萬，敬兒皆有之。

translations.literal: At this time the Wu household was registered and confiscated; only the family members came out naked, while servants, goods, and property worth tens of millions all came into Jing'er's possession.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu household was then registered and confiscated. Only the family members escaped naked, while servants, goods, and property worth tens of millions all fell to Jing'er.

sentences.zh: 先所通婢，即以為妾。

translations.literal: The maid with whom he had earlier had the affair he immediately made his concubine.
translations.idiomatic: The maid with whom he had earlier had the affair he immediately took as his concubine.

sentences.zh: 後為越騎校尉，桂陽王事起，隸齊高帝頓新亭。

translations.literal: Later he became Commandant of the Rapid-as-Leopards Cavalry; when the Prince of Guiyang's affair arose he was attached to Emperor Gao of Qi stationed at Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became Commandant of the Rapid-as-Leopards Cavalry. When the Prince of Guiyang's revolt broke out he served under Emperor Gao of Qi at Xinting.

sentences.zh: 賊矢石既交，休范白服乘輿勞樓下。

translations.literal: When the rebels' arrows and stones were already exchanged, Xiu Fan in white dress rode in a carriage to encourage the troops below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: As arrows and stones flew between the armies, Xiu Fan appeared in white dress in a carriage to encourage his troops below the tower.

sentences.zh: 敬兒與黃回白高帝求詐降以取之。

translations.literal: Jing'er and Huang Hui told Emperor Gao they wished to feign surrender in order to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er and Huang Hui asked Emperor Gao's permission to feign surrender in order to seize Xiu Fan.

sentences.zh: 高帝曰：「卿若辦事，當以本州相賞。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao said, "If you accomplish the affair, I shall reward you with your home province."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao said, "If you succeed, I shall reward you with your home province."

sentences.zh: 」敬兒相與出城南，放仗走，大呼稱降。

translations.literal: Jing'er went out together south of the city, cast aside their weapons and ran, and shouted loudly that they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er went out south of the city with his men, cast aside their weapons, ran forward, and shouted that they surrendered.

sentences.zh: 休範喜，召至輿側。

translations.literal: Xiu Fan was pleased and summoned them to the side of his carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu Fan was delighted and summoned them to the side of his carriage.

sentences.zh: 回陽致高帝密意，休範信之。

translations.literal: Hui conveyed Emperor Gao's secret intent, and Xiu Fan believed them.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui conveyed Emperor Gao's secret intent, and Xiu Fan believed them.

sentences.zh: 回目敬兒，敬兒奪取休范防身刀斬之，其左右百人皆散。

translations.literal: Hui signaled Jing'er with his eyes; Jing'er seized Xiu Fan's personal defense sword and cut him down, and his hundred-odd attendants all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hui signaled Jing'er with his eyes. Jing'er seized Xiu Fan's personal sword and cut him down, and his hundred-odd attendants scattered.

sentences.zh: 敬兒持首歸新亭。

translations.literal: Jing'er carried the head back to Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er carried the head back to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 除驍騎將軍，加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry general and additionally made Pacifying-the-State general.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Valiant Cavalry general and additionally made Pacifying-the-State general.

sentences.zh: 高帝置酒謂敬兒曰：「非卿之功無今日。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gao set out wine and said to Jing'er, "Without your merit there would be no today."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao set out wine and said to Jing'er, "Without your merit there would be no today."

sentences.zh: 高帝以敬兒人位既輕，不欲使便為襄陽重鎮。

translations.literal: Emperor Gao, because Jing'er's person and rank were still light, did not wish to let him at once hold the weighty post of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao, considering Jing'er's rank still too low, did not wish to place him immediately in the weighty post of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 敬兒求之不已，乃微動高帝曰：「沈攸之在荊州，公知其欲何所作，不出敬兒以防之，恐非公之利也。

translations.literal: Jing'er begged for it without cease and then subtly moved Emperor Gao, saying, "Shen Youzhi is in Jingzhou—you know what he intends to do; if you do not send Jing'er out to guard against him, I fear it will not be to your advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er begged without cease and then subtly urged Emperor Gao, saying, "Shen Youzhi is in Jingzhou—you know what he intends. If you do not send me out to guard against him, I fear it will not be to your advantage."

sentences.zh: 」帝笑而無言，乃除雍州刺史，加都督，封襄陽縣侯。

translations.literal: The emperor smiled and said nothing, then appointed him Governor of Yongzhou with the added title of Area Commander and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xiangyang county.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor smiled and said nothing, then appointed him Governor of Yongzhou with the added title of Area Commander and enfeoffed him as Marquis of Xiangyang county.

sentences.zh: 部伍泊沔口，敬兒乘舴艋過江，詣晉熙王燮。

translations.literal: His troops moored at Hankou; Jing'er took a skiff across the river to visit the Prince of Jinxi Xie Xie.
translations.idiomatic: His troops moored at Hankou. Jing'er took a skiff across the river to visit the Prince of Jinxi Xie Xie.

sentences.zh: 中江遇風船覆，左右丁壯者各泅水走，餘二小史沒船下求敬兒救，敬兒兩掖挾之，隨船仰得在水上，如此翻覆行數十里，方得迎接。

translations.literal: Mid-river he met wind and the boat capsized; the strong young men on his left and right each swam away, while two junior clerks submerged under the boat begged Jing'er to save them—Jing'er held one under each arm, followed the boat floating upward and got atop the water, thus overturning and proceeding for several tens of li before he was finally received.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-river a storm capsized the boat. The strong young men on either side swam away, while two junior clerks clung under the boat begging Jing'er to save them. He held one under each arm, kept himself atop the overturned boat, and drifted for several tens of li before he was rescued.

sentences.zh: 失所持節，更給之。

translations.literal: He lost the staff of authority he was carrying and was given another.
translations.idiomatic: He lost the staff of authority he was carrying and was given a replacement.

sentences.zh: 至鎮，厚結攸之，得其事蹟，密白高帝，終無二心。

translations.literal: Upon reaching his command he formed close ties with Youzhi, obtained intelligence on his activities, secretly reported to Emperor Gao, and in the end had no second heart.
