translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching his post he cultivated close ties with Youzhi, gathered intelligence on his activities, secretly reported to Emperor Gao, and never wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 又與攸之司馬劉攘兵情款。

translations.literal: He also had warm affection with Youzhi's headquarters marshal Liu Rangbing.
translations.idiomatic: He also formed a warm bond with Youzhi's headquarters marshal Liu Rangbing.

sentences.zh: 及蒼梧廢，敬兒疑攸之當因此起兵，密問攘兵，攘兵無所言，寄敬兒馬鐙一隻。

translations.literal: When Cangwu was deposed Jing'er suspected Youzhi would therefore raise troops; he secretly questioned Rangbing, who said nothing and sent Jing'er one horse stirrup.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei of Cangwu was deposed Jing'er suspected Youzhi would raise troops. He secretly questioned Liu Rangbing, who said nothing but sent Jing'er a single horse stirrup.

sentences.zh: 敬兒乃為備。

translations.literal: Jing'er then made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er then made preparations.

sentences.zh: 升明元年冬，攸之反，遣使報敬兒。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Shengming Youzhi rebelled and sent envoys to report this to Jing'er.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Shengming Youzhi rebelled and sent envoys to notify Jing'er.

sentences.zh: 勞接周至，為設食訖，列仗於聽事前斬之。

translations.literal: He received them with exhaustive courtesy, set out a meal for them, and when it was finished arrayed troops before the reception hall and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: He received them with exhaustive courtesy, entertained them at a meal, and when it was finished arrayed troops before the reception hall and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 集部曲。

translations.literal: He assembled his troops.
translations.idiomatic: He assembled his troops.

sentences.zh: 偵攸之下，當襲江陵。

translations.literal: Scouting below Youzhi, he was to strike Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Scouting Youzhi's movements, he prepared to strike Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒告變使至，高帝大喜，進號鎮軍將軍，改督。

translations.literal: When Jing'er's envoys reporting the rebellion arrived, Emperor Gao was greatly pleased and advanced his title to Pacifying-the-Army general with a change of area command.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing'er's envoys reporting the rebellion arrived, Emperor Gao was greatly pleased and advanced his title to Pacifying-the-Army general with a change of area command.

sentences.zh: 攸之至郢城敗走，其子元琰與兼長史江乂、別駕傅宣等還江陵。

translations.literal: Youzhi reached Yingcheng, was defeated, and fled; his son Yuan Yan, together with acting chief administrator Jiang Yi, vice-director Fu Xuan, and others returned to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi reached Yingcheng, was defeated, and fled. His son Yuan Yan, together with acting chief administrator Jiang Yi, vice-director Fu Xuan, and others returned to Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒軍至白水，元琰聞城外鶴唳，謂是叫聲，恐懼欲走。

translations.literal: When Jing'er's army reached Baishui, Yuan Yan heard cranes crying outside the walls and took it for human shouting; terrified, he wished to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing'er's army reached Baishui, Yuan Yan heard cranes crying outside the walls and mistook it for human shouting. Terrified, he prepared to flee.

sentences.zh: 其夜，乂、宣開門出奔，城潰，元琰奔寵洲見殺。

translations.literal: That night Yi and Xuan opened the gates and fled out; the city collapsed, Yuan Yan fled to Chongzhou and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jiang Yi and Fu Xuan opened the gates and fled. The city fell apart, and Yuan Yan fled to Chongzhou where he was killed.

sentences.zh: 敬兒至江陵，誅攸之親黨，沒入其財物數千萬，善者悉以入私，送台者百不一焉。

translations.literal: Jing'er reached Jiangling, executed Youzhi's kin and partisans, and confiscated property worth tens of millions; what was good he all took for himself, and what was sent to the court was not one in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er reached Jiangling, executed Youzhi's kin and partisans, and confiscated property worth tens of millions. The best items he kept for himself; scarcely one in a hundred was sent to the court.

sentences.zh: 攸之于湯渚村自經死，居人送首荊州。

translations.literal: Youzhi hanged himself at Tangzhu village, and the inhabitants sent his head to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi hanged himself at Tangzhu village, and the local people sent his head to Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬兒使楯擎之，蓋以青傘，徇諸市郭，乃送建鄴。

translations.literal: Jing'er had it borne on a shield, covered with a green umbrella, displayed through the market towns, and then sent to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er had it borne on a shield, covered with a green umbrella, paraded through the market towns, and then sent to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to duke.
translations.idiomatic: His noble rank was advanced to duke.

sentences.zh: 敬兒在雍州貪殘，人間一物堪用，莫不奪取。

translations.literal: Jing'er in Yongzhou was greedy and cruel; any usable object among the people, none was not seized.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzhou Jing'er was greedy and cruel. Any usable object among the people, he seized it.

sentences.zh: 於襄陽城西起宅，聚物貨，宅大小殆侔襄陽。

translations.literal: West of Xiangyang city he built a residence and amassed goods; the residence in size nearly matched Xiangyang itself.
translations.idiomatic: West of Xiangyang he built a mansion and amassed goods until the estate in size nearly rivaled the city itself.

sentences.zh: 又欲移羊叔子墮淚碑，於其處置台。

translations.literal: He also wished to move Yang Hu's Falling-Tears stele and set up a terrace in its place.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to move Yang Hu's Falling-Tears stele and build a terrace in its place.

sentences.zh: 綱紀諫曰：「此羊太傅遺德，不宜遷動。

translations.literal: The disciplinary officer remonstrated, saying, "This is the legacy virtue of Lord Yang the Grand Tutor—it is not fitting to move it."
translations.idiomatic: The disciplinary officer remonstrated, saying, "This is the legacy of Grand Tutor Yang—it must not be moved."

sentences.zh: 」敬兒曰：「太傅是誰，我不識。」

translations.literal: Jing'er said, "Who is the Grand Tutor? I do not know him."
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er said, "Who is the Grand Tutor? I do not know him."

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，轉侍中、中軍將軍，遷散騎常侍、車騎將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication he was transferred to Palace Attendant and General of the Army for the Center, then moved to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Chariots and Cavalry with staff aides appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication he was transferred to Palace Attendant and General of the Army for the Center, then to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry and General of Chariots and Cavalry with a full staff.

sentences.zh: 高帝崩，遺詔加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao died, his testamentary edict added the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao died, his testamentary edict granted him the privilege of an office equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 於家竊泣曰：「官家大老天子可惜，太子年少，向我所不及也。

translations.literal: At home he wept privately and said, "The old Son of Heaven of the house is a pity; the crown prince is young—he is not what I could match."
translations.idiomatic: At home he wept privately and said, "The old emperor is a pity. The crown prince is young—not the man I could have matched."

sentences.zh: 」及拜，王敬則戲之，呼為褚彥回。

translations.literal: When he went to receive the appointment Wang Jingze jested with him and called him Chu Yanhui.
translations.idiomatic: When he went to receive the appointment Wang Jingze teased him and called him Chu Yanhui.

sentences.zh: 敬兒曰：「我馬上所得，終不能作華林合勳也。

translations.literal: Jing'er said, "What I won on horseback—I could never become a Huailin joint merit-holder."
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er said, "What I won on horseback—I could never become one of those Huailin merit-holders."

sentences.zh: 」敬則甚恨焉。

translations.literal: Jingze hated this greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze took great offense.

sentences.zh: 初，敬兒微時，有妻毛氏，生子道門，而鄉里尚氏女有色貌，敬兒悅之，遂棄毛氏而納尚氏為室。

translations.literal: At first, when Jing'er was still obscure, he had a wife of the Mao clan who bore the son Daomen, but a daughter of the Shang clan in the village had beauty and looks—Jing'er was pleased with her, abandoned the Mao wife, and took the Shang woman as his principal wife.
translations.idiomatic: In his early days Jing'er had a wife of the Mao clan who bore the son Daomen, but a daughter of the Shang clan in his village was beautiful. Jing'er was smitten, abandoned Lady Mao, and took Lady Shang as his principal wife.

sentences.zh: 及居三司，尚氏猶居襄陽宅。

translations.literal: When he held one of the Three Excellencies the Shang woman still lived at the Xiangyang residence.
translations.idiomatic: Even after he held one of the Three Excellencies, Lady Shang still lived at the Xiangyang residence.

sentences.zh: 慮不復外出，乃迎家口悉下至都，啟武帝，不蒙勞問。

translations.literal: Fearing he would not go out again, he brought all his household down to the capital and reported to Emperor Wu, but received no gracious inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would never leave the capital again, he brought his entire household to the capital and reported to Emperor Wu, but received no gracious inquiry.

sentences.zh: 敬兒心自疑。

translations.literal: Jing'er inwardly grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 及垣崇祖死，愈恐懼。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chongzu died he grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chongzu was killed his fear only grew.

sentences.zh: 性好卜術，信夢尤甚，初征荊州，每見諸將帥，不遑有餘計，唯敘夢云：「未貴時，夢居村中，社樹欻高數十丈。

translations.literal: By nature he loved divination and especially trusted dreams; when he first went out to Jingzhou, whenever he saw the various generals and commanders he had no leisure for other talk but only told dreams, saying, "Before I was honored I dreamed I lived in a village and the community-tree suddenly grew several tens of zhang high."
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved divination and especially trusted dreams. When he first went out to Jingzhou, whenever he met the generals he had no time for anything else but to recount his dreams, saying, "Before I was honored I dreamed I lived in a village where the community tree suddenly grew several tens of zhang high."

sentences.zh: 及在雍州，又夢社樹直上至天。

translations.literal: When in Yongzhou he again dreamed the community-tree shot straight up to heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzhou he dreamed again that the community tree shot straight up to heaven.

sentences.zh: 」以此誘說部曲，自雲貴不可言。

translations.literal: With this he enticed and persuaded his troops, himself saying his honor was beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: With this he wooed his troops, declaring that his destiny was beyond words.

sentences.zh: 由是不自測量，無知。

translations.literal: Because of this he did not measure himself and was without understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he lost all sense of measure and judgment.

sentences.zh: 又使於鄉里為謠言，使小兒輩歌曰：「天子在何處？

translations.literal: He also had rumors made in his home village and had little boys sing, "Where is the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: He also spread rumors in his home village and had little boys sing, "Where is the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 宅在赤谷口，天子是阿誰？

translations.literal: "His residence is at Red Valley Mouth—who is the Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: "His residence is at Red Valley Mouth—who is the Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 非豬如是狗。

translations.literal: Not a pig but like a dog.
translations.idiomatic: Not a pig but like a dog.

sentences.zh: 」敬兒家在冠軍，宅前有地名赤穀。

translations.literal: Jing'er's family was in Guanjun, and before his residence was a place named Red Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er's family was in Guanjun, and before his residence was a place named Red Valley.

sentences.zh: 既得開府，又望班劍，語人曰：「我車邊猶少班蘭物。」

translations.literal: Once he had obtained the privilege of an equal office he also desired the ceremonial swords and told people, "Beside my carriage I still lack the class-lan objects."
translations.idiomatic: Once he had obtained the privilege of an equal office he also coveted the ceremonial swords and told people, "Beside my carriage I still lack the ceremonial guard."

sentences.zh: 敬兒長自荒遠，少習武事，既從容都下，又四方寧靖，益不得志。

translations.literal: Jing'er had long come from remote wilds and in youth practiced military affairs; once he was at ease in the capital and the four quarters were tranquil, he was all the more unfulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er had long come from remote borderlands and in youth knew only military affairs. Once he was settled in the capital and the realm was at peace, he grew all the more restless.

sentences.zh: 其妻尚氏亦曰：「吾昔夢一手熱如火，而君得南陽郡；

translations.literal: His wife Lady Shang also said, "I once dreamed one hand hot as fire, and my lord obtained Nanyang commandery;"
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Shang also said, "I once dreamed one hand hot as fire, and you obtained Nanyang commandery;"

sentences.zh: 元徽中，夢一髀熱如火，君得本州；

translations.literal: in the Yuanhui era I dreamed one thigh hot as fire and my lord obtained his home province;"
translations.idiomatic: in the Yuanhui era I dreamed one thigh hot as fire and you obtained your home province;"

sentences.zh: 建元中，夢半體熱，尋得開府；

translations.literal: in the Jianyuan era I dreamed half the body hot, and soon obtained the equal office;"
translations.idiomatic: in the Jianyuan era I dreamed half my body hot, and soon you obtained the equal office;"

sentences.zh: 今復舉體熱矣。

translations.literal: now again the whole body is hot."
translations.idiomatic: now my whole body is hot again."

sentences.zh: 」以告所親，言其妻初夢次夢，又言：「今舉體熱矣」。

translations.literal: She told those close to her of her wife's first dream, second dream, and again said, "Now the whole body is hot."
translations.idiomatic: She told her intimates of these dreams in sequence and again said, "Now my whole body is hot."

sentences.zh: 閹人聞其言說之，事達武帝。

translations.literal: Eunuchs heard her words and reported them; the affair reached Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs heard her words and reported them, and the matter reached Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 敬兒又遣使與蠻中交關，武帝疑有異志，永明元年，敕朝臣華林八關齋，於坐收敬兒。

translations.literal: Jing'er also sent envoys to maintain relations with the tribes; Emperor Wu suspected disloyal intent. In the first year of Yongming he ordered the court gentlemen to the Huailin Eight-Gates fast, and at the gathering seized Jing'er.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er also sent envoys to maintain relations with the tribes, and Emperor Wu suspected disloyal intent. In the first year of Yongming he ordered the court gentlemen to the Huailin Eight-Gates fast and seized Jing'er at the gathering.

sentences.zh: 初，左右雷仲顯常以盈滿誡敬兒，不能從，至是知有變，抱敬兒泣，敬兒脫冠貂投地曰：「用此物誤我。

translations.literal: At first his attendant Lei Zhongxian often warned Jing'er against fullness and excess, but he could not follow this; when he now knew there was trouble he embraced Jing'er and wept. Jing'er cast off his cap and sable to the ground and said, "These things have misled me."
translations.idiomatic: His attendant Lei Zhongxian had often warned him against excess, but he would not listen. When trouble came Lei embraced him and wept. Jing'er cast off his cap and sable to the ground and said, "These things have ruined me."

sentences.zh: 」及子道門、道暢、道休並伏誅，少子道慶見宥。

translations.literal: His sons Daomen, Daochang, and Daoxiu were all executed, while the youngest son Daoqing was spared.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Daomen, Daochang, and Daoxiu were all executed, while the youngest son Daoqing was spared.

sentences.zh: 後數年，上與豫章王嶷三日曲水內宴，舴艋船流至御坐前覆沒，上由是言及敬兒，悔殺之。

translations.literal: Several years later the emperor and the Prince of Yuzhang Xie held a three-day winding-water inner banquet; a skiff drifted before the imperial seat and capsized, and the emperor for this reason spoke of Jing'er and regretted killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the emperor and the Prince of Yuzhang Xie held a three-day winding-water banquet. A skiff drifted before the imperial seat and capsized, and the emperor spoke of Jing'er and regretted having killed him.

sentences.zh: 敬兒始不識書，及為方伯，乃習學讀孝經、論語。

translations.literal: Jing'er at first could not read; when he became a regional commander he then studied and read the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er at first could not read. When he became a regional commander he studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 初徵為護軍，乃潛於密室中屏人學揖讓答對，空中俯仰，妾侍竊窺笑焉。

translations.literal: When first summoned as Guardian of the Army he secretly in a sealed room dismissed others and practiced bowing, yielding, and answering; bowing up and down in empty space, while concubines and attendants peeked and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: When first summoned as Guardian of the Army he secretly practiced bowing, yielding, and court replies alone in a sealed room, bowing up and down to empty air while his concubines peeked in and laughed.

sentences.zh: 將拜三司，謂其妻嫂曰：「我拜後府開黃合。

translations.literal: When about to receive appointment among the Three Excellencies he said to his wife and sisters-in-law, "After I am appointed my headquarters will open the yellow gate."
translations.idiomatic: When about to receive appointment among the Three Excellencies he told his wife and sisters-in-law, "After I am appointed my headquarters will open the yellow gate."

sentences.zh: 」因口自為鼓聲。

translations.literal: He then made drum sounds with his mouth himself.
translations.idiomatic: He then beat out drum sounds with his mouth.

sentences.zh: 初得鼓吹，羞便奏之。

translations.literal: When he first obtained martial music he was ashamed and at once had it played.
translations.idiomatic: When he first obtained martial music he was embarrassed but had it played at once.

sentences.zh: 又于新林慈姥廟為妾祈子祝神，口自稱三公，其鄙俚如此。

translations.literal: He also at the Cimu Temple in Xinlin prayed to the god for a son on behalf of a concubine, calling himself one of the Three Excellencies with his own mouth—his vulgarity was like this.
translations.idiomatic: He also prayed at the Cimu Temple in Xinlin for a son on behalf of a concubine, calling himself one of the Three Excellencies aloud—such was his vulgarity.

sentences.zh: 始其母于田中臥，夢犬子有角舐之，已而有娠而生敬兒，故初名苟兒。

translations.literal: At the beginning his mother lay in the fields and dreamed a dog-pup with horns licked her; afterward she became pregnant and bore Jing'er, and so his first name was Gou'er.
translations.idiomatic: His mother once lay in the fields and dreamed a horned dog-pup licked her. She then became pregnant and bore Jing'er, who was first named Gou'er.

sentences.zh: 又生一子，因苟兒之名復名豬兒。

translations.literal: She bore another son and, following Gou'er's name, named him again Zhu'er.
translations.idiomatic: She bore another son and, following Gou'er's name, called him Zhu'er.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝嫌苟兒名鄙，改為敬兒，故豬兒亦改為恭兒，位正員郎，謝病歸本縣，常居上保村，不肯出仕，與居人不異。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song disliked the vulgarity of the name Gou'er and changed it to Jing'er; therefore Zhu'er was also changed to Gong'er. He held the post of regular gentleman and, citing illness, returned to his home county, regularly dwelling in Shangbao village, refusing to take office, no different from the local inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Song disliked the vulgarity of the name Gou'er and changed it to Jing'er, so Zhu'er was renamed Gong'er. He held the post of regular gentleman, cited illness, and returned to his home county, living in Shangbao village and refusing office, no different from the local people.

sentences.zh: 與敬兒愛友甚篤。

translations.literal: With Jing'er his affection and friendship were very deep.
translations.idiomatic: He and Jing'er were deeply devoted to each other.

sentences.zh: 及聞敬兒敗，走入蠻。

translations.literal: When he heard of Jing'er's defeat he fled into the tribal lands.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of Jing'er's defeat he fled into the tribal lands.

sentences.zh: 後首出，原其罪。

translations.literal: Later he came forward and surrendered; his crime was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Later he surrendered and was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 崔慧景

translations.literal: Cui Huijing
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing

sentences.zh: 崔慧景字君山，清河東武城人也。

translations.literal: Cui Huijing, styled Junshan, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Huijing, styled Junshan, was a native of Dongwucheng in Qinghe commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖構，奉朝請。

translations.literal: His grandfather Gou was a court gentleman attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Gou was a court gentleman attendant.

sentences.zh: 父系之，州別駕。

translations.literal: His father Xizhi was a provincial vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xizhi was a provincial vice-director.

sentences.zh: 慧景少有志業，仕宋為長水校尉。

translations.literal: Huijing from youth had ambition and enterprise; he served Song as Commandant of the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Huijing was ambitious. He served under Song as Commandant of the Long River.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝在淮陰，慧景與宗人祖思同時自結。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi was in Huaiyin, Huijing and his clansman Zusi at the same time attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi was in Huaiyin, Huijing and his clansman Zusi pledged themselves to him at the same time.

sentences.zh: 及高帝受禪，封樂安縣子，為都督、梁南秦二州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gao received the abdication he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Le'an county and made Area Commander and Governor of the two provinces Liang and Nanqin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao received the abdication he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Le'an county and appointed Area Commander and Governor of Liang and Nanqin provinces.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，為司州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming he became Inspector of Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming he became Inspector of Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 母喪，詔起復本任。

translations.literal: When his mother died an edict ordered him to resume his former post before mourning was complete.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died an edict ordered him to resume his former post before mourning was complete.

sentences.zh: 慧景每罷州，輒傾資獻奉，動數百萬。

translations.literal: Whenever Huijing left a province he would pour out his resources in tribute, often reaching millions.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Huijing left a province he poured out his wealth in tribute to the throne, often reaching millions.

sentences.zh: 武帝以此嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu for this reason praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 十年，為都督、豫州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he became Area Commander and Inspector of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Area Commander and Inspector of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，慧景以少主新立，密與魏通，朝廷疑之。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yulin took the throne Huijing, because the young lord was newly established, secretly communicated with Wei, and the court was suspicious of him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Yulin took the throne Huijing, seeing a young emperor newly enthroned, secretly communicated with Wei, and the court grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 明帝輔政，遣梁武帝至壽春安慰之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming was regent he sent Emperor Wu of Liang to Shouchun to reassure him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming was regent he sent Emperor Wu of Liang to Shouchun to reassure him.

sentences.zh: 慧景密啟送誠勸進。

translations.literal: Huijing secretly memorialized offering his sincerity and urging advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing secretly memorialized pledging his loyalty and urging the regent to advance.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，為度支尚書，領太子左率。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu he became Minister of Revenue and concurrently led the Left Guard of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwu he became Minister of Revenue and concurrently led the Left Guard of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 東昏即位，為護軍。

translations.literal: When Donghun took the throne he became Guardian of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Donghun took the throne he was appointed Guardian of the Army.

sentences.zh: 時輔國將軍徐世標專權號令，慧景備員而已。

translations.literal: At that time the Pacifying-the-State general Xu Shibiao monopolized authority and orders; Huijing was only a name on the roster.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Pacifying-the-State general Xu Shibiao monopolized power; Huijing was only a name on the roster.

sentences.zh: 帝既誅戮將相，舊臣皆盡，慧景自以年宿位重，轉不自安。

translations.literal: Since the emperor had executed generals and ministers and old officials were all gone, Huijing considered himself aged in years and weighty in rank and grew ever less at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Since the emperor had executed generals and ministers and the old officials were gone, Huijing, aged and high in rank, grew ever more uneasy.

sentences.zh: 及裴叔業以壽陽降魏，即授慧景平西將軍，假節、侍中、護軍如故。

translations.literal: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouyang to Wei he was at once given Huijing as General Who Pacifies the West, with borrowed staff, Palace Attendant, and Guardian of the Army as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Shuye surrendered Shouyang to Wei, Huijing was at once appointed General Who Pacifies the West, with borrowed staff, retaining his posts as Palace Attendant and Guardian of the Army.

sentences.zh: 率軍水路征壽陽。

translations.literal: He led the army by water route to campaign against Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: He led the army by water to campaign against Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 軍頓白下將發，帝長圍屏除，出琅邪城送之。

translations.literal: The army halted at Baixia about to set out; the emperor had the long screens removed and went out from Langye city to see him off.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Baixia about to set out. The emperor had the long screens removed and went out from Langye city to see him off.

sentences.zh: 帝戎服坐樓上，召慧景騎進圍內，無一人自隨，裁交數言，拜辭而去。

translations.literal: The emperor in military dress sat on the tower, summoned Huijing to ride into the enclosure, not a single person following him on his own; they exchanged only a few words, bowed in leave-taking, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in military dress sat on the tower and summoned Huijing to ride into the enclosure alone. They exchanged only a few words before Huijing bowed and departed.

sentences.zh: 慧景出至白下甚喜，曰：「頸非復小豎等所折也。

translations.literal: Huijing went out to Baixia very pleased and said, "This neck is no longer something those little boys can break."
translations.idiomatic: Huijing left for Baixia greatly pleased and said, "This neck is no longer something those little boys can break."

sentences.zh: 」子覺為直合將軍，慧景密與之期。

translations.literal: His son Jue was a direct-gate general; Huijing secretly made an appointment with him.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jue was a direct-gate general, and Huijing secretly made an appointment with him.

sentences.zh: 時江夏王寶玄鎮京口，聞慧景北行，遣左右余文興說之曰：「朝廷任用群小，猜害忠賢，江、劉、徐、沈，君之所見，身雖魯、衛，亦不知滅亡何時。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Jiangxia Bao Xuan garrisoned Jingkou; hearing Huijing was marching north he sent his attendant Yu Wenxing to persuade him, saying, "The court employs a crowd of petty men and suspects and harms the loyal and worthy—Jiang, Liu, Xu, Shen, as you have seen; though one be like Lu or Wei, one still does not know when destruction will come."
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Jiangxia Bao Xuan garrisoned Jingkou. Hearing Huijing was marching north he sent his attendant Yu Wenxing to persuade him, saying, "The court employs petty men and suspects and harms the loyal—Jiang, Liu, Xu, Shen, as you have seen. Though one be as secure as Lu or Wei, one still cannot know when ruin will come."

sentences.zh: 君今段之舉，有功亦死，無功亦死，欲何求所免。

translations.literal: My lord, in this present expedition, with merit you die, without merit you die—what do you seek by which to escape?
translations.idiomatic: In this expedition, with merit you die, without merit you die—what do you seek by which to escape?

sentences.zh: 機不可失，今擁強兵，北取廣陵，收吳、楚勁卒；

translations.literal: The opportunity cannot be lost; now holding a strong army, take Guangling in the north and gather the stalwart troops of Wu and Chu;
translations.idiomatic: The opportunity cannot be lost. Now that you hold a strong army, take Guangling in the north and gather the stalwart troops of Wu and Chu;

sentences.zh: 身舉州以相應，取大功如反掌耳。

translations.literal: I shall raise my province to respond—to achieve great merit is like turning the hand on its back.
translations.idiomatic: I shall raise my province to join you—great merit will be as easy as turning your hand over.

sentences.zh: 」慧景常不自安，聞言回應。

translations.literal: Huijing was often ill at ease and, hearing these words, responded in agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing was often ill at ease and, hearing these words, agreed.

sentences.zh: 于時廬陵王長史蕭寅、司馬崔恭祖守廣陵城，慧景以寶玄事告恭祖。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Luling's chief administrator Xiao Yin and headquarters marshal Cui Gongzu guarded Guangling city; Huijing told Gongzu of Bao Xuan's affair.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Luling's chief administrator Xiao Yin and headquarters marshal Cui Gongzu guarded Guangling. Huijing told Gongzu of Bao Xuan's plan.

sentences.zh: 恭祖先無宿契，口雖相和，心實不同。

translations.literal: Gongzu had had no prior bond with him; though their mouths agreed, their hearts were truly not the same.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu had no prior bond with him. Though he agreed in words, his heart was not in it.

sentences.zh: 還以事告寅，共為閉城計。

translations.literal: He returned and told Yin of the affair, and together they made a plan to close the city.
translations.idiomatic: He returned and told Yin, and together they planned to shut the city gates.

sentences.zh: 寅心謂恭祖與慧景同，謂曰：「廢昏立明，人情所樂，寧可違拒。

translations.literal: Yin in his heart thought Gongzu was of one mind with Huijing and said to him, "To depose the benighted and establish the enlightened is what human feeling delights in—how can one refuse?"
translations.idiomatic: Yin assumed Gongzu was of one mind with Huijing and said to him, "To depose the benighted and establish the enlightened is what all men desire—how can we refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」恭祖猶執不同。

translations.literal: Gongzu still held to disagreement.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu still refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而慧景至，恭祖閉門不敢出。

translations.literal: Shortly Huijing arrived; Gongzu closed the gates and did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huijing arrived. Gongzu shut the gates and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 慧景知其異己，泣數行而去。

translations.literal: Huijing knew he was not of his party; weeping several lines he departed.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing knew he was not with him, wept, and departed.

sentences.zh: 中兵參軍張慶延、明岩卿等勸慧景襲取廣陵，及密遣軍主劉靈運間行突入。

translations.literal: The central army aide Zhang Qingyan, Ming Yanqing, and others urged Huijing to seize Guangling by surprise, and secretly sent the army commander Liu Lingyun by a hidden route to burst in.
translations.idiomatic: Central army aide Zhang Qingyan, Ming Yanqing, and others urged Huijing to seize Guangling by surprise and secretly sent army commander Liu Lingyun by a hidden route to burst in.

sentences.zh: 慧景俄系至，遂據其城。

translations.literal: Huijing shortly arrived in bonds and then occupied the city.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing soon arrived and occupied the city.

sentences.zh: 子覺至，仍使領兵襲京口。

translations.literal: His son Jue arrived and was at once sent to lead troops in a surprise attack on Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jue arrived and was at once sent to lead troops in a surprise attack on Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 寶玄本謂大軍並來，及見人少，極失所望，拒覺，擊走之。

translations.literal: Bao Xuan had originally thought the great army would all come; when he saw few men he was utterly disappointed, rejected Jue, and struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Xuan had expected the full army to come. When he saw only a small force he was bitterly disappointed, rejected Jue, and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 恭祖及覺精兵八千濟江。

translations.literal: Gongzu and Jue with eight thousand picked troops crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu and Jue crossed the river with eight thousand picked troops.

sentences.zh: 恭祖心本不同反，至蒜山，欲斬覺以軍降京口，事既不果而止。

translations.literal: Gongzu in his heart had never agreed to rebellion; reaching Suanshan he wished to behead Jue and surrender the army to Jingkou, but when the affair did not succeed he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu had never agreed to rebellion. Reaching Suanshan he wished to behead Jue and surrender the army to Jingkou, but when the plan failed he abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 覺等軍器精嚴，柳憕、沈佚之等謂寶玄曰：「崔護軍威名既重，乃誠可見，既已唇齒，忽中道立異。

translations.literal: Jue and the others had weapons refined and strict; Liu Yun, Shen Yizhi, and others said to Bao Xuan, "The Guardian of the Army Cui's reputation for authority is already weighty and his sincerity can be seen; since we are already lip and teeth, to stand apart midway is strange."
translations.idiomatic: Jue's troops were well armed. Liu Yun, Shen Yizhi, and others said to Bao Xuan, "Guardian of the Army Cui's reputation is formidable and his sincerity is plain. We are already bound together—why break apart midway?"

sentences.zh: 彼以樂歸之眾，亂江而濟，誰能拒之。

translations.literal: They with troops glad to return, crossing the river in disorder—who can refuse them?
translations.idiomatic: They cross the river with troops eager for victory—who can stop them?

sentences.zh: 」於是登北固樓，並千蠟燭為烽火，舉以應覺。

translations.literal: Thereupon they ascended the Beigu tower, joined a thousand wax candles as beacon fire, and raised it to respond to Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they ascended the Beigu tower, lit a thousand wax candles as beacon fires, and signaled to Jue.

sentences.zh: 帝聞變，以右衛將軍左興盛假節、督都下水陸眾軍。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of the change and made the Right Guard general Zuo Xingsheng bearer of borrowed staff to command all land and water forces below the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of the revolt and made Right Guard general Zuo Xingsheng bearer of borrowed staff to command all land and water forces below the capital.

sentences.zh: 慧景停二日，便率大眾一時俱濟江，趣京口，寶玄仍以覺為前鋒，恭祖次之，慧景領大都督為眾軍節度。

translations.literal: Huijing halted two days, then led the great mass all at once to cross the river together, pressing toward Jingkou; Bao Xuan again made Jue the vanguard, Gongzu second, and Huijing as Grand Commander directed all the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing halted two days, then led his entire force across the river at once toward Jingkou. Bao Xuan made Jue the vanguard, Gongzu second, and Huijing as Grand Commander directed all the armies.

sentences.zh: 東府、石頭、白下、新亭諸城皆潰，左興盛走，不得入宮，逃淮渚荻船中，慧景禽殺之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Headquarters, Shitou, Baixia, Xinting, and all the cities collapsed; Zuo Xingsheng fled, could not enter the palace, escaped among reed boats on the Huai shallows, and Huijing captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Headquarters, Shitou, Baixia, Xinting, and all the cities fell. Zuo Xingsheng fled, could not enter the palace, hid among reed boats on the Huai shallows, and Huijing captured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 慧景稱宣德皇后令，廢帝為吳王。

translations.literal: Huijing proclaimed an order in the name of the Empress Dowager of Xuande and deposed the emperor as Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing proclaimed an order in the name of the Empress Dowager of Xuande and deposed the emperor as Prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 時柳憕別推寶玄，恭祖為寶玄羽翼，不復承奉，慧景嫌之。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yun separately promoted Bao Xuan; Gongzu was Bao Xuan's wings and no longer submitted in service, and Huijing resented this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yun backed Bao Xuan separately. Gongzu served as Bao Xuan's wing and no longer obeyed Huijing, who resented this.

sentences.zh: 巴陵王昭胄先逃人間，出投慧景，意更向之，故猶豫未知所立，此聲頗泄。

translations.literal: The Prince of Baling Zhao Zhou had earlier fled among the people and came out to join Huijing; his intent turned more toward him, so he hesitated not knowing whom to establish, and this rumor leaked out somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Baling Zhao Zhou had earlier fled into hiding and came out to join Huijing. Huijing leaned toward enthroning him and hesitated, unsure whom to establish, and word of this leaked out.

sentences.zh: 憕、恭祖始貳于慧景。

translations.literal: Yun and Gongzu then became divided from Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun and Gongzu then turned against Huijing.

sentences.zh: 又恭祖勸慧景射火箭燒北掖樓，慧景以大事垂定，後若更造，費用功多，不從其計。

translations.literal: Gongzu also urged Huijing to shoot fire arrows and burn the North Wing Attendant tower; Huijing, because the great affair was nearly settled and rebuilding afterward would cost much labor, did not follow this plan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu also urged Huijing to shoot fire arrows and burn the North Wing Attendant tower. Huijing, thinking the great affair nearly settled and that rebuilding would cost too much labor, refused.

sentences.zh: 性好談義，兼解佛理，頓法輪寺，對客高談，恭祖深懷怨望。

translations.literal: By nature he loved discoursing on principles and also understood Buddhist doctrine; he halted at Falun Temple and discoursed loftily with guests, while Gongzu harbored deep resentment.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved philosophical discourse and understood Buddhist doctrine. He halted at Falun Temple and discoursed loftily with guests, while Gongzu harbored deep resentment.

sentences.zh: 先是，衛尉蕭懿為豫州刺史，自歷陽步道征壽陽，帝遣密使告之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Commandant of the Guards Xiao Yi was Inspector of Yuzhou and was marching from Liyang by land route to campaign against Shouyang; the emperor sent a secret envoy to inform him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Commandant of the Guards Xiao Yi, Inspector of Yuzhou, was marching from Liyang by land to campaign against Shouyang. The emperor sent a secret envoy to inform him.

sentences.zh: 懿率軍主胡松、李居士等自採石濟岸，頓越城舉火，台城中鼓叫稱慶。

translations.literal: Yi led the army commanders Hu Song, Li Jushi, and others across from Caishi, halted at Yuecheng and raised beacon fires, and within the capital city drums and shouts proclaimed celebration.
translations.idiomatic: Yi led army commanders Hu Song, Li Jushi, and others across from Caishi, halted at Yuecheng and raised beacon fires, and within the capital drums and shouts proclaimed celebration.

sentences.zh: 恭祖先勸慧景遣二千人斷西岸軍，令不得度，慧景以城旦夕降，外救自然應散，不許。

translations.literal: Gongzu first urged Huijing to send two thousand men to cut off the army on the west bank and prevent crossing; Huijing, because the city would surrender within days and outside relief would naturally disperse, did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu first urged Huijing to send two thousand men to block the army on the west bank. Huijing, thinking the city would surrender within days and outside relief would disperse on its own, refused.

sentences.zh: 恭祖請擊義師，又不許。

translations.literal: Gongzu requested to attack the loyalist army, and again this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu asked to attack the loyalist army, and again Huijing refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣子覺將精甲數千人度南岸，義師昧旦進戰，覺大敗。

translations.literal: He then sent his son Jue with several thousand picked armored men across the south bank; the loyalist army advanced to battle at dawn and Jue was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his son Jue with several thousand picked troops across the south bank. The loyalist army attacked at dawn and routed Jue.

sentences.zh: 慧景人情離沮。

translations.literal: Among Huijing's men morale separated and flagged.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing's men lost heart.

sentences.zh: 恭祖頓軍興皇寺，於東宮掠得女妓，覺來逼奪，由是忿恨。

translations.literal: Gongzu encamped his army at Xinghuang Temple, plundered female entertainers from the Eastern Palace, and when Jue came to seize them by force he harbored resentment for this.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu encamped at Xinghuang Temple and plundered female entertainers from the Eastern Palace. When Jue came to seize them by force he grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 其夜，崔恭祖與驍將劉靈運詣城降。

translations.literal: That night Cui Gongzu and the fierce general Liu Lingyun went to the city to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: That night Cui Gongzu and fierce general Liu Lingyun went to the city to surrender.

sentences.zh: 慧景乃將腹心數人潛去，欲北度江，城北諸軍不知，猶為拒戰。

translations.literal: Huijing then took several men of his inner circle and slipped away secretly, wishing to cross the river north; the various armies north of the city did not know and still fought in resistance.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing then slipped away secretly with several trusted men, intending to cross the river north. The armies north of the city did not know and still fought on.

sentences.zh: 城內出蕩，殺數百人，慧景餘眾皆奔。

translations.literal: The city sent out raiders and killed several hundred men; Huijing's remaining troops all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The city sent out raiders and killed several hundred men. Huijing's remaining troops all fled.

sentences.zh: 慧景圍城凡十二日，軍旅散在都下，不為營壘。

translations.literal: Huijing besieged the city for twelve days in all; his army was scattered through the capital and did not make encampments.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing besieged the city for twelve days in all. His troops were scattered through the capital and made no encampments.

sentences.zh: 及走，眾於道稍散，單馬至蟹浦，投漁人太叔榮之。

translations.literal: When he fled his troops gradually dispersed along the road; alone on horseback he reached Xiepu and threw himself on the fisherman Taishu Rongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: As he fled his men gradually dispersed along the road. Alone on horseback he reached Xiepu and threw himself on the fisherman Taishu Rongzhi.

sentences.zh: 榮之故為慧景門人，時為蟹浦戍，謂之曰：「吾以樂賜汝，汝為吾覓酒。

translations.literal: Rongzhi had formerly been Huijing's follower and was then garrisoned at Xiepu; he said to him, "I give you my music as a gift—you find wine for me."
translations.idiomatic: Rongzhi had formerly been Huijing's follower and was then garrisoned at Xiepu. He said to him, "I give you my belt as a gift—you find wine for me."

sentences.zh: 」既而為榮之所斬，以頭內魷籃中擔送都。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was beheaded by Rongzhi; his head was placed in a cuttlefish basket and carried to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Rongzhi beheaded him, placed his head in a cuttlefish basket, and carried it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 恭祖者，慧景宗人，驍果便馬韒，氣力絕人，頻經軍陣。

translations.literal: Gongzu was Huijing's clansman, fierce and bold, skilled with horse and saddle, his strength surpassing other men, and had repeatedly passed through battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzu was Huijing's clansman, fierce and bold, skilled with horse and saddle, of surpassing strength, and had seen many battles.

sentences.zh: 討王敬則，與左興盛軍容袁文曠爭敬則首，訴明帝曰：「恭祖禿馬絳衫，手刺倒敬則，故文曠得斬其首。

translations.literal: In campaigning against Wang Jingze he disputed with Zuo Xingsheng's army aide Yuan Wenkuan over Jingze's head and appealed to Emperor Ming, saying, "Gongzu in bald head, red horse, and crimson shirt personally stabbed and felled Jingze, and so Wenkuan was able to cut off his head."
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Wang Jingze he disputed with Zuo Xingsheng's army aide Yuan Wenkuan over Jingze's head and appealed to Emperor Ming, saying, "Gongzu, bareheaded on a red horse in a crimson shirt, personally stabbed and felled Jingze, so Wenkuan was able to cut off his head."

sentences.zh: 以死易勳而見枉奪。

translations.literal: I risked death for merit yet was wrongly deprived of it.
translations.idiomatic: I risked death for merit yet was wrongly deprived of it.

sentences.zh: 若失此勳，要當刺殺左興盛。

translations.literal: If I lose this merit I shall certainly stab and kill Zuo Xingsheng.
translations.idiomatic: If I lose this merit I shall certainly kill Zuo Xingsheng.

sentences.zh: 」帝以其勇健，謂興盛曰：「何容令恭祖與文曠爭功。

translations.literal: The emperor, because of his courage and vigor, said to Xingsheng, "How can one allow Gongzu and Wenkuan to dispute merit?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, impressed by his courage, said to Xingsheng, "How can we let Gongzu and Wenkuan dispute over merit?"

sentences.zh: 」慧景平後，恭祖系尚方，少時殺之。

translations.literal: After Huijing was pacified Gongzu was imprisoned in the Masters of Works, and shortly was killed.
translations.idiomatic: After Huijing's revolt was crushed Gongzu was imprisoned in the Masters of Works and soon executed.

sentences.zh: 覺亡命為道人，見執伏法。

translations.literal: Jue fled as a fugitive and became a Daoist priest; he was seized and executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Jue fled and became a Daoist priest. He was seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 覺弟偃，年十八便身長八尺，博涉書記，善蟲篆，為始安內史，藏竄得免。

translations.literal: Jue's younger brother Yan at eighteen was already eight chi tall, broadly versed in documents and records, skilled in seal script, served as Inner Scribe of Shi'an, hid in concealment and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Jue's younger brother Yan was already eight chi tall at eighteen, widely read in documents, skilled in seal script, and served as Inner Scribe of Shi'an. He hid and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 和帝西台立，以為甯朔將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor He established the Western Terrace he was made Ningshuo general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor He established the Western Terrace he was made Ningshuo general.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，詣公車尚書申冤，言多指斥，尋下獄死。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he went to the Masters of Carriages to declare his grievance; his words were largely accusatory, and soon he was imprisoned and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing he went to the Masters of Carriages to declare his grievance. His words were largely accusatory, and soon he was imprisoned and died.

sentences.zh: 先是，東陽女子婁逞變服詐為丈夫，粗知圍棋，解文義，遍遊公卿，仕至揚州議曹從事。

translations.literal: Earlier, the woman Lou Cheng of Dongyang changed her dress and pretended to be a man, knew go roughly, understood literary meaning, traveled among dukes and ministers everywhere, and served up to Attendant of the Deliberation Office of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a woman named Lou Cheng of Dongyang disguised herself as a man. She knew go roughly, understood literary texts, traveled among the great families, and rose to Attendant of the Deliberation Office of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 事發，明帝驅令還東。

translations.literal: When the affair came out Emperor Ming drove her to return east.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was exposed Emperor Ming sent her back east.

sentences.zh: 逞始作婦人服而去，歎曰：「如此之伎，還為老嫗，豈不惜哉。

translations.literal: Cheng first put on woman's dress and departed, sighing, "With such skills, to return to being an old woman—is it not a pity?"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng put on women's dress again and departed, sighing, "With such talents, to return to being an old woman—is that not a pity?"

sentences.zh: 」此人妖也。

translations.literal: This person was a demon.
translations.idiomatic: This person was an omen of disorder.

sentences.zh: 陰而欲為陽，事不果故泄，敬則、遙光、顯達、慧景之應也。

translations.literal: Yin wishing to become yang—the affair did not succeed and therefore leaked out; this was the correspondence of Jingze, Yaoguang, Xianda, and Huijing.
translations.idiomatic: Yin wishing to become yang—the affair failed and was exposed; this was the omen fulfilled by Jingze, Yaoguang, Xianda, and Huijing.

sentences.zh: 舊史裴叔業有傳，事終於魏，今略之云。

translations.literal: The old history had a biography of Pei Shuye, whose affair ended in Wei; it is now omitted in brief.
translations.idiomatic: The old history had a biography of Pei Shuye, whose story ended in Wei; it is omitted here.

sentences.zh: 論曰：光武功臣所以能終身名者，豈唯不任職事，亦以繼奉章、明，心存正嫡。

translations.literal: The discussion says: The reason the meritorious ministers of Emperor Guangwu could preserve their names to the end of life was not only that they did not hold office duties, but also that they continued to serve Zhang and Ming and kept in mind the legitimate heir.
translations.idiomatic: Discussion: The meritorious ministers of Emperor Guangwu preserved their reputations to the end not only because they stepped back from office, but also because they continued to serve the Zhang and Ming emperors and upheld the legitimate succession.

sentences.zh: 王、陳拔跡奮飛，則建元、永明之運，身極鼎將，則建武、永明之朝。

translations.literal: Wang and Chen rose from humble tracks and soared—this was the fortune of Jianyuan and Yongming; their persons reached the pinnacle as generals and ministers in the courts of Jianwu and Yongming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang and Chen rose from humble origins in the age of Jianyuan and Yongming, and reached the pinnacle of power as generals and ministers in the courts of Jianwu and Yongming.

sentences.zh: 勳非往時，位踰昔等，禮授雖重，情分不交。

translations.literal: Their merit was not as in former times, their posts exceeded past ranks; ceremonial grants were heavy but emotional bonds did not join.
translations.idiomatic: Their merit did not match that of earlier times, their posts exceeded past ranks, ceremonial honors were lavish, but emotional bonds were never formed.

sentences.zh: 加以主猜政亂，危亡慮及，舉手扞頭，人思自免。

translations.literal: Added to this, the ruler was suspicious and government chaotic, thoughts of peril and ruin reached them, and raising hands to ward the head, each man thought to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, the ruler was suspicious and government chaotic. With ruin in sight, every man raised his hands to his head and thought only of saving himself.

sentences.zh: 干戈既用，誠淪犯上之跡，敵國起於同舟，況又疏於此也。

translations.literal: Once weapons were employed, they truly fell into traces of violating superiors; enemies arose from those in the same boat—how much more when estranged even from this?
translations.idiomatic: Once arms were taken up, they truly became rebels. Enemies arose even among those in the same boat—how much more when even that bond was gone?

sentences.zh: 敬兒挾震主之勇，當鳥盡之運，內惑邪夢，跡涉覬覦，其至殲亡，亦其理也。

translations.literal: Jing'er, relying on the courage that awes the ruler, met the fortune of when the birds are spent, inwardly deluded by evil dreams, his traces touching covetous longing—to reach annihilation was also according to reason.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er, relying on the courage that awes the ruler, met the fortune of when the bow is unstrung, was inwardly deluded by evil dreams, and showed the marks of ambition—to be destroyed was only to be expected.

sentences.zh: 慧景以亂濟亂，能無及乎。

translations.literal: Huijing used disorder to aid disorder—how could he escape the same end?
translations.idiomatic: Huijing used disorder to answer disorder—how could he escape the same end?
